HireHawk is a fast-growing staffing and recruitment solutions company helping businesses build high-performing teams through both onshore and offshore hiring support. We partner with companies across multiple industries to solve hiring challenges, improve recruiting efficiency, reduce operational friction, and connect them with rigorously vetted talent.

HireHawk goes beyond traditional staffing by supporting the full hiring infrastructure companies need to scale, including recruiting, talent sourcing, payroll coordination, compliance support, onboarding workflows, and ongoing workforce management.

About the Role

This is a hands-on outbound GTM and sales execution role for someone who can build, manage, and continuously improve a scalable outbound engine.

The Outbound GTM Lead will own the infrastructure, workflows, and day-to-day systems required to keep HireHawk’s SDR team operating at full capacity. This includes lead list creation, prospect segmentation, contact enrichment, Apollo workflows, call prioritization, CRM processes, SDR enablement, call review, outbound reporting, and multichannel campaign development.

The immediate priority for this role is to strengthen and scale HireHawk’s phone-based outbound motion by ensuring SDRs consistently have high-quality, relevant prospects to call, clear scripts and qualification criteria, structured follow-up processes, and actionable coaching based on call performance.

As the outbound engine matures, this role will also build and optimize additional outbound channels, including email and LinkedIn, to support or independently generate qualified opportunities.

This is not a pure marketing role and not a traditional Account Executive role. The focus is on building the systems, processes, messaging, and SDR execution required to generate more qualified meetings and create a predictable outbound pipeline.

The Outbound GTM Lead will work closely with SDRs, sales leadership, and account management to ensure HireHawk’s outbound motion is structured, measurable, repeatable, scalable, and aligned with our staffing and recruitment services.

Responsibilities:

Outbound Infrastructure & List Building

  • Build, optimize, and manage HireHawk’s outbound infrastructure across Apollo, CRM systems, sales engagement tools, data enrichment platforms, and reporting systems.
  • Own lead list creation, prospect segmentation, contact enrichment, phone-number validation, sequence setup, and outbound campaign execution.
  • Develop high-quality prospect lists segmented by ICP, industry, buyer persona, geography, company size, hiring activity, hiring signals, and staffing need.
  • Ensure SDRs consistently have sufficient volumes of high-quality, phone-ready prospects to maintain strong daily calling activity.
  • Build repeatable systems for sourcing, enriching, validating, prioritizing, and routing leads to SDRs.
  • Continuously improve list quality based on connect rates, conversation quality, meeting conversion, and SDR feedback.
  • Identify and test new prospecting signals, data sources, and enrichment methods that improve outbound performance.

SDR Enablement & Call Performance

  • Partner closely with SDRs to improve daily outbound execution, call prioritization, productivity, follow-up discipline, and qualified meeting conversion.
  • Regularly review SDR call recordings and live call performance to identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Provide actionable feedback and coaching on call openings, value propositions, qualification, objection handling, follow-up, and meeting conversion.
  • Develop and continuously improve cold-call scripts, talk tracks, objection-handling frameworks, and follow-up cadences.
  • Track recurring objections and market feedback and use those insights to improve targeting, messaging, scripts, and campaign strategy.
  • Help establish realistic activity and conversion benchmarks for SDR performance.
  • Build repeatable SDR playbooks, SOPs, workflows, training materials, and call-review processes.

Outbound Strategy & Multichannel Growth

  • Build and optimize outbound workflows across cold calling, email, LinkedIn, and CRM-based follow-up.
  • Prioritize channels based on measurable business impact rather than activity alone.
  • Initially focus on strengthening HireHawk’s phone-based outbound engine before scaling additional outbound channels.
  • Develop email and LinkedIn outbound programs once the core SDR calling process is operating effectively.
  • Determine when email and LinkedIn should function as follow-up and air-cover channels versus independent lead-generation channels.
  • Develop persona-specific and industry-specific messaging based on buyer pain points, market feedback, and campaign performance.
  • Run structured outbound experiments across ICPs, messaging, channels, call scripts, and hiring signals.

Analytics, Reporting & Process Improvement

Analyze SDR activity and outbound campaign performance across:

  • dials
  • connect rates
  • conversations
  • positive conversations
  • meetings booked
  • show rates
  • qualified meetings
  • qualified opportunities
  • conversion rates
  • performance by list, persona, industry, and campaign
  • Identify where outbound conversion is breaking down across list quality, targeting, messaging, call execution, follow-up, or qualification.
  • Build and maintain dashboards that make outbound performance clear and actionable.
  • Use performance data to continuously improve lists, scripts, workflows, SDR execution, and campaign strategy.
  • Maintain CRM hygiene, accurate lead stages, follow-up tasks, campaign attribution, and reporting discipline.
  • Reduce unnecessary manual work through automation while maintaining high data quality and strong SDR execution.

Requirements

  • Previous experience in a staffing agency, recruitment firm, RPO, talent acquisition company, HR services business, or workforce solutions company.
  • Strong hands-on experience building and managing outbound prospecting workflows using Apollo or similar sales intelligence and engagement platforms.
  • Demonstrated experience creating, enriching, validating, segmenting, and prioritizing outbound prospect lists.
  • Strong understanding of outbound cold calling, SDR workflows, call prioritization, prospecting sequences, follow-up cadences, and qualified meeting generation.
  • Experience working directly with SDRs or BDRs and improving their performance through call review, coaching, scripts, objection handling, and process development.
  • Ability to analyze outbound funnel performance and identify whether problems are caused by targeting, list quality, messaging, call execution, follow-up, or qualification.
  • Experience building or improving outbound sales systems and processes from the ground up.
  • Experience creating multichannel outbound campaigns across phone, email, LinkedIn, and CRM-based follow-up.
  • Strong understanding of staffing and recruitment buyer personas, pain points, objections, and sales motions.
  • Experience creating outbound messaging, cold-call scripts, email copy, LinkedIn messaging, and objection-handling frameworks.
  • Experience using AI and automation tools to improve list quality, prospect research, hiring-signal identification, segmentation, personalization, campaign development, and workflow efficiency.
  • Strong analytical and operational mindset with the ability to translate outbound performance data into practical improvements.
  • Highly organized, process-driven, and comfortable operating independently in a fast-paced startup environment.
  • Comfortable joining live sales calls, listening to SDR recordings, reviewing call notes, and providing direct performance feedback.
  • Comfortable being hands-on with execution rather than operating only at a strategy or management level.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with HubSpot, Salesforce, Outreach, Salesloft, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo, Clay, Instantly, Smartlead, Zapier, Make, or similar GTM tools.
  • Experience managing or supporting high-volume cold-calling environments.

  • Familiarity with AI-assisted lead research, enrichment, segmentation, call analysis, and messaging workflows.

What success looks like:

  • Call scripts, objection handling, qualification criteria, and follow-up processes are clearly documented and actively improving.
  • SDR calls are reviewed regularly and coaching is tied to measurable performance data.
  • Outbound reporting clearly identifies where conversion is succeeding or breaking down.

Within the first 90 days:

  • Manual list-building requirements have been significantly reduced.
  • SDR productivity and qualified meeting generation have improved.
  • Clear outbound playbooks and SOPs are in place.

jobs.title: Database Migrations Engineer - EMEA
jobs.excerpt: Laravel is the most popular PHP framework in the world.
jobs.description:
Laravel is the most popular PHP framework in the world. 500M+ lifetime downloads. Thousands of packages. A developer community that shows up at conferences, in forums, on Twitter, in Discord servers, in every "what framework should I use?" thread on the internet.

But Laravel is more than a framework. It's a complete platform. From choosing a stack, to building an app, to deploying it, monitoring it, and scaling it. Laravel Cloud is our managed PaaS, and enterprise customers moving onto it face a common, stubborn blocker: database migration. We need someone who solves that problem directly.

Why This Job Is Unique

You will be on calls with enterprise customers and you will run the migration with them. Not routing tickets. Not advising from a distance. Actually owning the technical execution alongside the customer - which matters most when we sign a large, impactful contract and need to deliver.

You are picking up a real, ongoing function. There is existing database migration work that needs an owner - including the PlanetScale relationship and recurring ad-hoc requests scattered across channels. You are not starting from zero.

The brief is to build the muscle, not wait for the full menu. Rather than first defining every database we will ever offer, you are the one who develops the function in practice. You’ll be learning what customers need, productising the repeatable parts, and making the case for what comes next.

You will seed what you know. The model is "immediate pain relief, then the whole team gets better." Documentation, runbooks, and lightweight training so Sales, CS and engineering compound on your expertise rather than staying dependent on it.

What the Database Migrations Engineer Will Do

  • Execute database migrations with enterprise and Private Cloud customers. Sit on calls, own the technical execution, and deliver successful migrations for customers onboarding to Laravel Cloud - primarily MySQL and Postgres.
  • Assume ownership of the PlanetScale relationship and migration work. Take over this function from its current ad-hoc state and run it cleanly and autonomously.
  • Productise repeatable migration patterns. Identify the most common downtime-tolerant migrations and package them - documentation, decision logic, edge cases - so they stop being bespoke. We want repeatability over heroics — and with an eye towards eventually bringing that knowledge in-product, whether through documentation, wizards, or self-serve flows, so that product-led customers can benefit too.
  • Automate recurring migration requests. Map the one-off requests that surface repeatedly across channels and eliminate the manual effort.
  • Own broader app and service migrations in the gaps. Act as a generalist migration resource for application and service migrations onto Private Cloud when database migration work permits.
  • Distribute what you learn. Write clearly. Build runbooks. Create reference material that makes Sales, CS and engineering better without making them dependent on you.
  • Keep the database offering competitive. Stay close to the market — monitoring what alternatives like PlanetScale, Aurora, and Percona offer in terms of pricing, instance classes, and capabilities. Flag proactively when our offering is out of step with what customers are seeing elsewhere, and advise on what needs to change.

Requirements

What We Are Looking For

  • Genuine strength across both MySQL and Postgres. We are deliberately optimising for ~80% capability in each over 100% in one. Database specialists tend to plant a flag, and we need coverage across both camps.
  • Direct experience with database migrations in a customer-facing capacity. You have been on the calls, you have run the process alongside engineers and customers, and you are comfortable owning the technical execution rather than advising on it.
  • A productisation instinct. You see the repeatable pattern inside bespoke work and know how to package it without over-engineering.
  • Strong written and async communication. We are fully remote and documentation is how knowledge compounds.
  • Comfort operating in a role where part of the scope is yours to define. There is a clear immediate need, and you will also be shaping what the function looks like from here.

Nice to Have

  • Experience at a database tooling or infrastructure company - PlanetScale, Percona, Vitess, or similar
  • Experience building tooling or automation around migration workflows
  • Familiarity with AWS-based infrastructure or PaaS environments
  • Experience with AWS DMS or comparable migration tooling — DMS has a role in certain migrations and prior use is a strong signal of hands-on production database migration experience
  • A track record of writing, speaking, or teaching publicly about database topics
  • Some familiarity with PHP applications

Benefits

  • Work From Home
  • Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
  • Paid Time Off (Vacation, Sick & Public Holidays)
  • Family Leave (Maternity, Paternity)
  • Stock Option Plan

jobs.title: Lead Site Reliability Engineer - Canada, Remote (CA)
jobs.excerpt: Our TeamThe Incident Response Team sits at the intersection of every customer-impacting failure across Vista.
jobs.description:
Our Team

The Incident Response Team sits at the intersection of every customer-impacting failure across Vista. We coordinate response to critical incidents, drive learning out of every event, and partner with engineering teams across the organisation to make Vista more reliable. Today the team is strong on incident handling, and we are deliberately raising the engineering bar to match.

What You Will Do

  • Identify patterns of failure across the organisation. Analyse incidents and post-incident reviews to find the recurring technical root causes behind customer impact, rather than treating each incident as a one-off.

  • Prioritise the biggest improvement levers. Focus reliability effort where it most reduces Mean Time to Detect and Mean Time to Resolve, and where it proactively prevents the next incident from happening at all.

  • Turn those patterns into the right engineering intervention and influence the teams who can build it. This includes safe deployment defaults, secret and credential rotation, resilience patterns such as circuit breakers and fallbacks, observability and alerting standards, contract testing, and infrastructure pre-flight validation. You drive the what and the why; the owning teams build it.

  • Help teams hands-on, in their code, through Merge Requests, pairing, code review, and active technical support, favouring the simplest intervention that prevents recurrence over the most elaborate one.

  • Disseminate and evangelise improvements across the organisation. Identify best practices, document them, and transfer the learning to other teams so that local fixes become shared practice and improvements compound rather than stay siloed.

  • Lead the technical conversation in post-incident reviews and operational forums. Ask the questions that surface missing monitoring, untested failure modes, incomplete rollback strategies, and unaddressed dependency risks, and steer toward the simplest solution that holds.

  • Help the Incident Response Team grow its engineering practice by pairing on real work, sharing what good engineering looks like in our context, and running internal learning sessions that bring the team from incident-response specialists toward incident-response engineers.

  • Partner across teams without direct authority. Work with Platform Engineering, Deployment Platform, Developer Productivity, and senior engineers across Vista; contribute as a reviewer on proposals that touch reliability, deployment safety, observability, or operational readiness; and take part in the team's on-call rotation, contributing incident leadership when shared coverage requires it.

Your Qualifications

At VistaPrint, we are striving to hire individuals that add new ideas and perspectives to our teams and enhance our culture. No matter your background or work experience, we strongly encourage you to apply—even if you feel that you don’t meet the exact requirements or have the same qualifications. You might be a great candidate for this or other opportunities.

  • 5 or more years of hands-on Site Reliability, Platform, or Infrastructure Engineering experience in a large-scale, distributed production environment, with proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, Go, TypeScript, Java) and a track record of code shipped to production

  • Demonstrated experience driving adoption of a reliability or platform pattern (e.g., progressive delivery, observability standard, resilience library, secret rotation) across teams that did not report to you, with measurable outcomes.

  • Strong systems thinking and a demonstrable bias toward simple solutions - able to read an incident or a design and identify the underlying class of problem (retries, cascading failures, queueing behaviour, partial failures, head-of-line blocking) and the smallest, cheapest intervention that addresses it. Comfortable choosing a post-deploy curl check over a full sandbox environment when the simpler intervention would prevent the same incident.

  • Hands-on experience with the modern reliability stack: at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure), an observability platform (for example New Relic, Datadog, or Grafana), defining and operating against Service Level Objectives, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, and infrastructure-as-code (for example AWS CDK, Pulumi).

  • Hands-on exposure to Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Model tooling in an engineering context, for example integrating Large Language Models into workflows or operational tooling, or using Artificial Intelligence meaningfully in your own engineering.

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience formally mentoring engineers, running internal learning programmes, or growing the engineering capability of a team that started from a non-engineering baseline.

  • Experience designing or running chaos engineering, GameDays, or failure-injection programmes.

  • Experience working in a globally distributed engineering organisation with Follow-the-Sun or 24/7 coverage models.

  • Experience integrating with or extending modern incident management and service-catalogue tooling (e.g., incident.io, PagerDuty, Cortex, Backstage) at the API or workflow level - not just as a user.

  • Experience building internal developer platforms, paved-road tooling, or "golden path" patterns that other engineering teams adopt by choice.

Why You'll Love Working Here

There is a lot to love about working at VistaPrint. We are an award winning Remote-First company. We’re an inclusive community. We’re growing (which means you can too). And to help orient us all in the same direction, we have our Vista Behaviors which exemplify the behavioral attributes that make us a culturally strong and high-performing team.

About Us

VistaPrint is the design and marketing partner to millions of small businesses around the world. For over 20 years we’ve been inspired by small businesses, and we work incessantly to deliver solutions to their evolving needs. Together, VistaCreate, 99designs by Vista and VistaPrint represent a full-service design, digital and print solution, elevating small businesses’ presence in physical and digital spaces and powering them to achieve success. VistaPrint is focused on making great marketing and design accessible to every small business owner, allowing them to create a cohesive brand image for use in-store, online and on-the-go.

Commitment to Diversity, Equity, & Inclusion

VistaPrint exists to help our customers live their dreams. Each dream is unique – and the VistaPrint team needs to be as well. We believe in the unique contributions of everyone within a diverse global organization. We are collaborative, inclusive, and innovative. We strive to role model and live an inclusive culture of fairness, respect and belonging for all. And we work together to empower each other, creating a space in which each of us can spark our next great idea.

Equal Opportunity Employer

BrandActive specializes in the financial analysis, strategy, and logistics of rebrand implementation. Since 1998, we’ve helped many of the world’s most valuable brands plan, budget, and implement brand change—optimizing spend, improving efficiency, and reducing complexity along the way.

Our work combines industry-leading analytics with a proven methodology to help clients make smarter decisions, save time and money, and get more value from their brand investments—whether they’re navigating a major rebrand or managing their brand day to day. You can explore examples of our work in our case studies.

At BrandActive, we’re committed to building an inclusive, supportive workplace where people can do their best work and grow together. We strive to set the global standard for excellence in our industry while fostering a culture rooted in trust, agility, and growth —guided by our North Star: great people, doing great work, and having a great time doing it.

The Opportunity

We’re looking for a highly organized, process-minded Growth Operations leader who can turn strategic priorities into coordinated action across an integrated sales and marketing team. You’ll bring structure, visibility, and follow-through to how the team operates, leading cross-functional initiatives, creating and strengthening processes and systems, and ensuring teams have the clarity, information, and tools they need to execute effectively.

Responsibilities

Growth operational planning and performance

  • Acts as the operational driver behind strategic goals set by SVP, Growth, translating priorities into coordinated actions across campaigns, partnerships, sales initiatives, and internal workflows to ensure consistent execution and follow-through.

  • Owns day-to-day coordination of partnership activities, including tracking next steps, maintaining partner documentation and mapping, supporting partner meetings and follow-ups, and helping identify opportunities to deepen strategic partner engagement.

Strategic initiatives and cross-functional enablement

  • Leads and project manages strategic Growth Operations initiatives, including HubSpot improvements and transformation, operationalization of the community advocacy program, and industry research and advancement initiatives, coordinating stakeholders and maintaining visibility from planning through delivery.

  • Identifies bottlenecks and creates systems to eliminate them, building repeatable processes that reduce manual effort and solve cross-functional friction.

  • Bring forward smarter, faster, better solutions to processes and identify opportunities to be more agile in day-to-day activities.
  • Demonstrate inclusive and supportive behavior, contributing to BrandActive’s core values of trust, agility, and growth, commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion, (EDI), humanity, and wellbeing.

Qualifications and Experience

This role is for someone who thinks about Growth Operations holistically—how an integrated sales and marketing team works together, how priorities move across functions, and how the right processes, systems, information, and operating rhythms enable the team to perform. It is not a traditional Marketing Operations or technology-focused role; while tools such as HubSpot and project management platforms are important enablers, the focus is on improving how the broader Growth team operates.

You might not tick every box, but if you meet most of the qualifications and are excited about the role, we’d love to hear from you. We value potential, curiosity, and a growth mindset.

  • Strong project and program management skills, with experience translating strategic priorities into structured plans and coordinating multiple workstreams through execution.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, align stakeholders, and drive clear ownership, decisions, and follow-through.
  • Strong ability to manage up by anticipating needs, proactively surfacing risks and decisions, and providing leadership with clear visibility into progress and priorities.
  • Experience shaping and improving project management systems, processes, and ways of working to increase team effectiveness and reduce friction.
  • Strong facilitation and communication skills, with the ability to lead productive meetings and working sessions across teams and levels of seniority.
  • Highly organized and process-minded, with strong judgment, initiative, and the ability to identify roadblocks and bring forward practical solutions.
  • Strong analytical and reporting skills, with the ability to consolidate information, identify meaningful insights, and support data-informed decision-making.
  • Comfortable working across CRM, reporting, project management, and collaboration platforms; experience with HubSpot and using automation or AI to improve workflows is critical.

  • Flexible work options – Remote (open to BC, Alberta, Ontario provinces) with adaptable schedules.
  • Two annual town halls in Toronto, featuring engaging sessions and fun team activities.
  • Supportive leadership and career development, with ongoing coaching and feedback to help you grow and succeed, quarterly formal feedback, annual performance reviews and separate annual development meetings.

AGBO is looking for a SeniorRendering Engineer to join the team and sit at the intersection of cinematic storytelling and real-time technology, pushing the visual boundaries of what's possible in interactive experiences tied to some of the most ambitious IP in entertainment. If you're driven by the challenge of making real-time graphics feel like they belong on a cinema screen, this role was built for you.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own the technical vision and architecture for the entire rendering pipeline, making high-stakes tradeoffs between visual fidelity, performance, and platform constraints that shape the project's creative direction
  • Set the technical bar for advanced rendering techniques -- global illumination, ray tracing, physically-based shading, post-processing, and VFX integration -- evaluating academic and industry research and determining what translates to shippable, production-ready features
  • Partner closely with Art and Technical Art leadership to define material workflows, lighting standards, and asset pipelines, directly shaping how the project balances visual ambition against hardware reality
  • Architect and own the rendering pipeline for real-time interactive experiences, designing systems that deliver cinematic visual fidelity at performance targets across target platforms

  • Represent the studio's rendering technology point of view externally and internally -- evaluating emerging API's, hardware capabilities, and platform-specific features, and building the case for adoption where it serves project goals.
  • Research, prototype, and implement advanced rendering techniques — including global illumination, ray tracing, physically-based shading, post-processing, and VFX integration — translating cutting-edge academic and industry work into shippable features
  • Collaborate closely with Art and Technical Art teams to define material workflows, lighting standards, and asset pipelines that maximize visual quality within hardware constraints
  • Contribute to engine-level tooling and editor workflows, building or extending rendering tools that empower artists and designers to iterate faster and with greater creative freedom
  • Partner with cross-functional leads in engineering, production, and creative to scope rendering features, communicate technical tradeoffs, and align on priorities across the project lifecycle
  • Stay ahead of the curve by evaluating emerging APIs, hardware capabilities (e.g., DirectX 12 Ultimate, Vulkan, Metal), and platform-specific rendering features, advocating for their adoption where they serve project goals
  • Perform all other duties as assigned

Qualifications & Skills:

  • 7+ years of professional experience in real-time rendering engineering within games, interactive entertainment, or a related field, with a strong portfolio of shipped titles or interactive experiences
  • Demonstrated experience owning rendering architecture end-to-end -- not just implementing features, but making and defending the foundation technical decisions a team builds on
  • Deep expertise in graphics APIs (Vulkan, DirectX 12, Metal, or OpenGL) and a solid command of at least one major real-time engine such as Unreal Engine 5, including experience working at the engine/renderer level
  • Mastery of c++ and shader languages (HLSL,GLSL, WGSL) with a track record of writing and reviewing high-performance, maintainable, production-grade rendering code at scale
  • Proven experience with advanced rendering techniques — physically-based rendering, deferred rendering, temporal anti-aliasing, screen-space effects, and/or ray tracing — and the ability to architect these systems from the ground up
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with a track record of working effectively in multidisciplinary teams and translating complex technical concepts for non-engineering stakeholders in a fast-moving, creative production environment

jobs.title: Marketing Designer
jobs.excerpt: Portcast is a venture-backed, Singapore-based logistics technology company building AI-powered intelligence for the freight forwarding industry.
jobs.description:
Portcast is a venture-backed, Singapore-based logistics technology company building AI-powered intelligence for the freight forwarding industry. Freight forwarders manage thousands of shipments, rates, exceptions, and operational decisions every day. The challenge is not a lack of data. It is knowing what needs attention, what is going wrong, and what action to take next.

Portcast uses AI and data to help freight forwarders surface shipment exceptions, identify cost and margin risks, and make better decisions across the shipment lifecycle. Our products help teams improve operational efficiency, protect margins, and make faster, more informed decisions. Our vision is to become the AI data and intelligence layer that powers exception management and margin improvement on every shipment.

Founded in 2018 and backed by leading technology investors, we are a lean, globally distributed team building technology for an industry going through a major digital transformation.

ABOUT THE ROLE:
We are looking for a Marketing Designer to be the design engine behind our marketing. You'll turn briefs and copy into polished, on-brand assets across the full funnel, landing pages, case studies, social and paid creative, event materials, product collateral, and video, often at speed and across several formats at once. You'll partner closely with content and growth marketing (copy and content sit with the Content Marketing Manager; the visual craft is yours) to keep a consistent visual system across everything we publish, and raise the bar on how the Portcast brand shows up.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

  • A consistent, high-quality visual system across everything Portcast publishes, with assets shipped quickly and on-brand across web, print, social, paid, and video, so marketing can move fast without design becoming a bottleneck or losing craft.

WHAT YOU’LL OWN:

  • Design landing pages, case study PDFs, product one-pagers, and sales/product collateral.
  • Produce social creative (LinkedIn-first), including post series and campaign templates.
  • Build paid media and creative for LinkedIn and Google campaigns across personas.
  • Create event and webinar assets: banners, booth graphics, decks.
  • Produce and edit video content end to end, short-form social clips, product feature videos, webinar/event recaps, and launch teasers, from raw footage to polished, on-brand output.
  • Maintain and extend the Portcast brand system: components, tokens, templates.
  • Support HTML email/newsletter production and light web design handoff.
  • Iterate quickly across multiple design and content review rounds.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

  • Bachelor's or Master's in Marketing, Business, or a related field, or equivalent.
  • At least 3+ years in a design role, ideally in-house at a B2B SaaS product-based startup or at an agency doing B2B marketing, with a portfolio that shows real range across web, print, social, campaign, and video work.
  • Fast, high-craft execution: You produce polished work quickly, often across several formats at once, without letting speed erode quality. You take direction and iterate well, but you hold your own opinions on what "good" looks like.
  • Detail-obsessed: Pixel alignment, spacing, and consistency matter to you. You catch the small things others miss and hold the visual bar across everything that ships.
  • Figma (advanced): You work fluently with components, variants, auto-layout, and shared libraries, and you keep the design system clean and reusable.
  • Adobe Creative Suite: Strong in Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign, including multi-page, print-ready layouts for case studies and collateral.
  • Design fundamentals: A strong grasp of typography, layout, grid systems, and brand consistency, and the ability to design for web and print formats interchangeably.
  • Creative at scale: You're comfortable designing social and paid ad creative at volume from templates, keeping everything on-brand across personas and campaigns.
  • Video editing and production: You can take a project from raw footage to finished, high-quality output, cutting, pacing, color, captions/subtitles, motion titles, and sound. You're fluent in Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects (or equivalent DaVinci Resolve / Final Cut), and CapCut or similar for fast short-form social edits.
  • Web and email handoff: A basic understanding of HTML/CSS, enough to work within existing markup for email and web handoff, not necessarily coding from scratch.
  • Brand systems: Working knowledge of brand systems and design tokens, and how to keep every asset on-system as the brand scales.
  • Advanced motion design: animation and motion work (Lottie, complex After Effects, 3D/Blender).
  • Presentation design: high-polish decks in PowerPoint or Google Slides.
  • AI design tooling: familiarity with image generation, AI-assisted layout, prompt-based workflows, and AI video.
  • Webflow basics: building or maintaining pages in Webflow, not just designing them.
  • Curiosity for the logistics domain: Experiencein logistics, supply chain, transportation, or freight technology is valued, but so is a genuine curiosity to understand our market in depth.
  • AI-forward mindset: You consistently apply AI across design workflows and actively experiment with new tools as they emerge.
  • Startup builder mentality: You thrive in lean, fast-moving environments where ownership is high and resources are limited.
  • Strong communicator: You communicate clearly across a diverse, distributed, cross-cultural team. You can be opinionated, but you engage with other views and compromise when it's right.

WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU:

    • Own the visual craft end to end: You'll own how Portcast looks and feels across everything we publish, with real influence over the brand and few layers between an idea and what ships.

    • Build in an industry still defining modern B2B marketing: Logistics and supply chain tech is at an exciting stage of digital transformation, with significant room to rethink how enterprise software is marketed and how it looks. You'll bring fresh ideas, challenge conventional thinking, and help shape what great design looks like in this space.

    • Work at the intersection of AI, design, and logistics: We have a strong product, established enterprise customers, and a real opportunity to sharpen how we show up. You'll get to push AI-forward design and video workflows, not just execute templates.

    • Small by design, fully distributed across Asia and Europe, built on trust, accountability, and collaboration. Your work directly shapes launches, customer perception, and how the market sees Portcast.

OUR CORE VALUES GUIDE EVERYTHING WE DO:

    • Curiosity: We dig into why a design worked or didn't, how a freight forwarder actually operates, and what makes our brand land with customers.

    • Ownership: We act like founders. We don't wait to be told what to make, and we stay on a piece until it's genuinely on-brand and right.

    • Raising the bar: We don't settle for assets that are merely fine. We hold a high standard for craft, polish, and the experience our brand creates.

    • Effectiveness: We focus on design that drives real marketing outcomes, pipeline, launches, and brand perception, not just output. We prioritize the right work and make practical trade-offs.

      • Join us at Portcast and help shape the future of the logistics and shipping industry through design that is as sharp as the product behind it.

Tanium is looking for a Senior Security Engineer to join the Customer Transparency team within the R&D Security organization, which protects the software and cloud services our customers depend on.

Tanium's customers secure some of the most consequential networks in the world and they extend us a great deal of trust. The Customer Transparency team is responsible for making Tanium's security posture something our customers can understand and act on, rather than something they have to blindly trust.

As a Senior Security Engineer on the Customer Transparency team, you will represent Tanium’s R&D Security organization to our external stakeholders. You will be responsible for our vulnerability disclosure program, developing a deep understanding of customers’ security needs, and taking action to drive these to resolution.

  • Identify what customers can't see about their own Tanium deployment and partner with Engineering and Product stakeholders to close those gaps
  • Oversee the SBOM and vulnerability management program and provide appropriate visibility to internal and external stakeholders
  • Collaborate with Customers, Partners, and Tanium's Customer organization to learn what customers actually need, treat recurring questions as engineering problems, and build the systems that solve them

About Gnosis Pay
Gnosis Pay provides the API and card-program infrastructure that enables wallets, fintechs, and businesses to issue stablecoin-powered payment cards and create custom payment flows. Partners can easily connect on-chain wallets to real-world spending.

Transactions are executed through a secure smart-wallet rather than a traditional bank account, allowing users to retain full custody of their assets while paying anywhere Visa is accepted.

We are looking for a Senior Business Development & Partnerships Manager with deep, traditional fintech experience to lead our expansion into the mainstream financial ecosystem. This role bridges Gnosis Pay's cutting-edge payment infrastructure with top-tier fintechs, neobanks, remittance providers, and platforms.

The ideal candidate brings an established, active network of payment decision-makers across digital banking, payroll, trading, and e-money institutions. While our core infrastructure leverages Web3, we strongly prefer a candidate from a traditional payments background (e.g., card issuers, processors, networks) who can translate complex infrastructure capabilities into compelling commercial partnerships for traditional fintech players.

Location

Who We Are
DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers operate in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production.
Delivering DoiT Cloud Intelligence, the only solution that integrates advanced technology with human intelligence, we help our customers solve complex multicloud problems and drive efficiency.
With decades of multicloud experience, we have specializations in Kubernetes, GenAI, CloudOps, and more. An award-winning strategic partner of AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, we work alongside more than 4,000 customers worldwide.

The Opportunity
The Engineering Manager is a hands-on, player-coach leadership role. You are embedded with your team - daily standup, code review, architectural calls, delivery planning, and performance management - and you own both the team's output and the team's growth.
This is a genuinely technical & leadership role. You are expected to write and review code, be a credible voice in architectural decisions, and stay current in your team's stack. You lead by demonstrating you can do the work at the highest level, not by title alone.The balance between hands-on contribution and leadership depends on the team's context, but your overarching mandate is the same: run the team, execute and deliver, and grow its impact.
Build the bench, raise the standard, and keep the operating cadence sharp as the work and the organization evolve. You work AI-augmented yourself, expect the same from your team, and push the team's craft forward with every new capability that lands.

Responsibilities
Team leadership & growth

  • Leading a team of engineers, owning both its delivery and its development.
  • Lead a mindset and process of continuous improvement within the team and meaningfully impact the team’s success over time. Small, compounding improvements, delivered via fast iterations, are the operating rhythm we expect, not an aspiration.
  • You are responsible for the professional well-being and career development of team members. Develop engineers through regular 1:1s, growth plans, performance reviews, and direct, candid feedback.
  • Develop the next layer of leadership - tech leads, senior engineers ready to manage, and ICs ready to step into staff roles.

    Technical leadership
  • Write code and review code. Be a credible voice in technical decisions because you have hands in the work, not because of your title - you are current, not rusty.
  • Drive the team's architectural and technical design decisions in partnership with senior ICs, ensuring alignment on approach and implementation.
  • Uphold engineering standards through thorough, constructive pull-request review and a healthy release process, keeping the team's components scalable and in a healthy state.
  • Work AI-augmented and lead an AI-augmented team, applying sharp judgment about where AI helps and holding the same quality bar for what ships.

    Roadmap & delivery
  • Own the team's commitments - what was promised, when it was promised, and the quality bar that was held.
  • Run a disciplined cadence of planning, prioritization, and delivery without becoming a process bureaucrat.
  • Partner closely with the Technical Product Owner and Product team on scope, sequencing, and tradeoffs, maintaining a roadmap that reflects both near-term priorities and longer-term direction.
  • Understand the broader business objectives behind the work, translate that context for the team, and ensure engineering effort clearly aligns with those objectives.
  • React decisively to change - re-planning, re-prioritizing, and re-staffing as the business moves - while keeping the team engaged and steady through the shift.

    Hiring
  • Own hiring for your team. Interview thoughtfully, decide quickly, and refuse to lower the bar to fill seats.
  • Recruit, coach, and - when needed - make hard calls toward the standard the team is held to.
  • Operate as a role model for other engineering managers across the organization: share your operating model, mentor peers, and raise the management bench.
  • Day-to-day communication & collaborationUpwards: Communicate clearly and succinctly, giving leadership the right level of context and prioritizing escalations based on relevant, well-gathered information.
  • Downwards: Empower senior engineers to own key areas of the product, and coach team members to stay focused, intentional, and aware of their impact.
  • Sideways: Partner effectively with Product, Design, GTM, Customer Success, and other teams - raising challenges and opportunities constructively to support cross-team alignment.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of engineering experience, including 4+ years in engineering management roles where you actively coded as part of your responsibilities.
  • Hands-on, real-life experience building cloud-based SaaS products - running services in production for Azure (and ideally additionally on AWS/GCP) , and owning availability, cost, and the customer-facing surface
  • Strong background in understanding and leading teams in the FinOps space.
  • API first mindset, products are built not just for end user experience through UI,they are fully functional and available through APIs, so both humans and agents can interact with the platform.
  • Strong background in engineering management of multi-disciplinary teams, including full-stack engineers and data engineers.
  • A track record of taking an engineering team and visibly transforming it - measurable improvements in delivery velocity, technical quality, or team caliber.
  • Deep technical fluency in your team's primary stack. You can read, write, and review code at a senior level, and you are current - not rusty.
  • Strong opinions on how high-performing engineering teams operate, and a clear philosophy on hiring, coaching, performance management, and technical decision-making.
  • Excellent judgment under pressure. You make calls quickly with imperfect information, communicate them clearly, and take responsibility for the outcomes.
  • Direct, candid communication. You give hard feedback well, and you hear it well.

    Bonus Points
  • Strong Golang knowledge or experience
  • A strong, already-established AI-augmented workflow, with opinions on how to apply AI tools and agentic workflows to raise both velocity and quality.
  • Hands-on experience with more than a single cloud provider.
  • Background in scaling teams, processes, or technical systems as the organization grows.

Are you a Do’er?
Be your truest self. Work on your terms. Make a difference.
We are home to a global team of incredible talent who work remotely and have the flexibility to have a schedule that balances your work and home life. We embrace and support leveling up your skills professionally and personally.
What does being a Do’er mean? We’re all about being entrepreneurial, pursuing knowledge, and having fun! Click here to learn more about our core values.

Sounds too good to be true? Check out our Glassdoor Page.
We thought so too, but we’re here and happy we hit that ‘apply’ button.

  • Parental Leave
  • Employee Stock Option Plan
  • Home Office Allowance
  • Professional Development Stipend
  • Peer Recognition Program

Many Do’ers, One Team
DoiT unites as Many Do’ers, One Team, where diversity is more than a goal—it's our strength. By celebrating differences, we create an environment where every individual feels valued, contributing to our collective success.

jobs.title: Product Builder
jobs.excerpt: Product builder 🌍 Global SaaS | $28M Series B Investment 📍 Remote in EuropeThe MissionMost product ideas die in the gap between "someone should look at this" and "a squad has capacity next cycle.
jobs.description:
Product builder

🌍 Global SaaS | $28M Series B Investment 📍 Remote in Europe

The Mission

Most product ideas die in the gap between "someone should look at this" and "a squad has capacity next cycle." As a Product Builder, you close that gap by being the whole loop yourself: you find the problem, talk to the users, build the thing, ship it, and read the result.

You own the path from problem to outcome. Not just the spec. Not just the ticket. The whole thing.

This is not a Product Manager who writes some code, and it is not an engineer who sits in on discovery calls. It's a single role that holds discovery and delivery in the same head, and uses AI to make that possible at a speed a three-person trio can't match on exploratory work. You'll work in the messy, high-ambiguity spaces around our Core Platform Product, our AI Voice Agents, Calling Apps and our product-led surfaces - the friction nobody owns, the repeated support question, the idea that's too early for a squad to commit a cycle to and too valuable to drop.

Our empowered squads own our committed roadmap and they're good at it. You own the things that haven't earned a squad yet. A good week for you isn't "I shipped a lot." It's "we now know something we didn't know on Monday, and there's working software proving it."


Key Responsibilities

1. Own the problem before anyone has written it down

  • Find the friction. You go looking - in support tickets, in churn calls, in the questions that keep landing in #product, in the gaps between two teams' surfaces. You don't wait for a brief.
  • Sharpen it into a hypothesis. Vague frustration becomes a falsifiable statement with a metric attached, fast enough that the sharpening doesn't become the project.
  • Talk to users yourself. Continuous discovery is not a phase you schedule. You're in contact with real customers weekly, and you can run an interview that surfaces behaviour rather than feature requests.
  • Run several bets in parallel. You explore three or four opportunities at once, then converge on the one or two worth real investment.

2. Build and ship it

  • End-to-end delivery. Prototype, build, test, ship to production, instrument. You work across the stack and you make your own design calls - there is no PM or Designer assigned to you, though both are a Slack message away and you use them well.
  • Ship small and early. You'd rather have something imperfect in front of five real customers this week than something complete in front of nobody next month.
  • Hold the quality line. Shipping fast is not shipping sloppy. You write tests, you think about failure modes, and you know when a prototype must not be allowed to become production.
  • Build AI-native, not AI-bolted-on. LLM-driven flows, agentic workflows and orchestration - you understand the models well enough to design around what they actually do, including what they get wrong.

3. Read the result and decide

  • Instrument before you ship. You define what would prove you wrong before the code goes out.
  • Kill your own ideas. You can look at a two-week build, see it didn't move the number, and shut it down without needing anyone's permission or a retro to justify it. This is the hardest part of the job and the one we'll dig into hardest in interviews.
  • Hand off deliberately. When something works and needs to scale, you write it up, transfer it to the owning squad, and walk away. You do not accumulate a personal estate of unowned production services.

4. Work AI-first, and make it count

  • AI as a multiplier, not the point. You use agentic workflows to compress the loop from idea to shipped. You can explain which tool for which job and why, and you know when the agent is confidently wrong.
  • Systems, not prompts. Repeatable workflows for research synthesis, prototyping, and experiment readouts - not one-off chats. Validation designed in.
  • Raise the floor. The patterns you find get written down and shared. Your leverage should show up in other people's throughput, not just your own.

5. Stay connected while working alone

  • Visible by default. You work with high autonomy, which means you over-communicate. What you're exploring, what you learned, what you killed, all in the open.
  • Commercially honest. You can explain what a bet is worth to the business in ARR, retention, or cost terms, and you can say "this isn't worth building" out loud.
  • A good citizen of the roadmap. You don't parachute into a squad's surface without talking to them. Discovery you run in their domain gets handed to them.|
    The Ideal Profile
    • The Full-Loop Operator. You have personally taken something from "I noticed a thing" to "customers are using it in production" - and you can name the metric that moved.
    • The AI-Fluent Builder. You re-engineer how work happens with AI (Level 4 on CloudTalk's AI fluency ladder). You ship things to production that would previously have needed a whole trio. You'll be asked for receipts.
    • The Comfortable Killer. You've shut down your own work. You can talk about a bet that failed, what it cost, what it taught you, and how fast you called it.
    • The Discovery Practitioner. Continuous discovery in the Teresa Torres sense is how you work, not a framework you've read about. You've run enough interviews to know how badly a leading question can poison a week of work.
    • The Ambiguity Native. Startup, founding, or scale-up background. You've worked without a spec, without a designer, and without anyone telling you what success looks like. You prefer it.
    • The B2B SaaS Realist. You understand a sales-assisted and PLG motion, an ARR-driven model, and the difference between a feature a customer asks for and a problem worth solving.

Nice to have: voice, telephony, or real-time systems experience. Founding or solo-technical-founder background. A public trail of things you've built.


Success Metrics (First 90 Days)

jobs.excerpt: Nosso Modo de Fazer no Time:Transforme sua carreira com o iFood!
jobs.description:
Nosso Modo de Fazer no Time:

Transforme sua carreira com o iFood! Somos uma empresa brasileira de tecnologia referência na América Latina. Por meio de soluções inovadoras, conectamos milhares de restaurantes a milhões de consumidores diariamente com uma média de 100 milhões de pedidos mensais. Além do delivery de comida, também somos Mercado, Farmácia e Pet. Temos também o iFood Pago, nossa Fintech, que engloba o iFood Benefícios, o vale alimentação e refeição do iFood e o próprio iFood Pago, o banco do restaurante. Junte-se a nós e faça parte de uma equipe que está sempre à frente com tecnologia de ponta e inovação constante.

Seu Cardápio Diário:

  • Liderar o desenho e a evolução de arquiteturas de segurança AWS-first em um ecossistema tecnológico de grande escala, garantindo que plataformas, workloads, ambientes Kubernetes, fluxos de dados e serviços críticos sejam seguros por design, resilientes por padrão e escaláveis por automação.
  • Atuar como principal referência técnica em Cloud Security, em parceria com Cloud Platform, SRE, Engenharia, Produto, Privacidade, Compliance, Detecção e Resposta e Arquitetura.
  • Traduzir riscos complexos em decisões técnicas pragmáticas, guardrails escaláveis e prioridades claras de remediação.
  • Definir e manter arquiteturas de referência, paved roads, padrões reutilizáveis e controles automatizados para ambientes AWS, incluindo estratégia multicloud, IAM, segmentação de redes, proteção de dados, logging, detecção de ameaças, prontidão para incidentes e padrões seguros de deployment.
  • Liderar revisões de arquitetura e threat modeling para produtos cloud-native críticos, APIs, pipelines de dados, workloads Kubernetes, arquiteturas orientadas a eventos e integrações relacionadas a AI/ML.
  • Identificar caminhos de ataque, limites de confiança, cenários de abuso, permissões excessivas e lacunas sistêmicas de controle antes da entrada em produção.
  • Ser responsável pela evolução dos padrões de identidade, acesso, Kubernetes, containers e redes, incluindo least privilege, credenciais temporárias, acesso Just-in-Time, workload identity, SCPs, RBAC, admission control, policy as code, gestão de segredos, detecção em runtime, WAF, proteção contra DDoS, segurança entre serviços e redução de blast radius.
  • Fortalecer detecção e resposta em cloud, definindo padrões de telemetria, casos de uso de detecção, runbooks, fluxos automatizados de contenção e integrações com SIEM/SOAR, CNAPP, CSPM, CI/CD e serviços nativos da AWS.
  • Construir e escalar automações de segurança por meio de infraestrutura como código, policy as code, detection as code, módulos Terraform seguros, guardrails de CI/CD, remediação orientada a eventos e mecanismos de self-service.
  • Mentorar engenheiros, especialistas de segurança, times de Plataforma e Security Champions, elevando o nível técnico em arquitetura segura, AWS Security, Kubernetes Security, automação, threat modeling e aprendizado pós-incidente.

Ingredientes Que Buscamos:

  • Conhecimento de nível especialista em arquitetura de segurança AWS, incluindo AWS Organizations, IAM Identity Center, SCPs, permission boundaries, IAM Access Analyzer, padrões de Landing Zone, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub, Config, Inspector, Macie, KMS, Secrets Manager, WAF, Shield, CloudFront, Route 53, VPC, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, EventBridge, Security Lake e logging centralizado.
  • Experiência profunda com IAM, incluindo least privilege, acesso federado, credenciais temporárias, JIT/JEA, workload identity, governança de acesso privilegiado, revisões de acesso, desenho de políticas e remediação de roles superprivilegiadas.
  • Experiência avançada em segurança de Kubernetes e containers, especialmente AWS/EKS, incluindo EKS, ECR, Helm, IRSA/pod identity, RBAC, admission controllers, OPA/Gatekeeper, Kyverno, políticas de rede, gestão de segredos, image scanning, runtime security e isolamento de workloads.
  • Conhecimento avançado de segurança de redes em cloud, incluindo desenho de VPC, roteamento, segmentação, controles de entrada e saída, security groups, NACLs, DNS, TLS/mTLS, WAF, proteção contra DDoS, CloudFront, service mesh, API gateways, análise de pacotes e logs e redução de movimentação lateral.
  • Experiência sólida com arquitetura segura, threat modeling, detecção e resposta em cloud, proteção de dados, gestão de vulnerabilidades, CNAPP/CSPM, policy as code, detection as code, Terraform, CI/CD, Python, Go, Bash e automação reutilizável de segurança.
  • Capacidade de liderar discussões técnicas, influenciar sem autoridade formal, comunicar riscos com clareza, construir consenso entre múltiplos times e equilibrar profundidade em segurança com velocidade de negócio.

Para Realçar o Sabor:

  • Experiência com desenho de estratégias de segurança cross-funcionais e automação de postura em múltiplos times.
  • Vivência com ambientes AWS e GCP ou outros ambientes multicloud.
  • Experiência com segurança de integrações de AI/ML e avaliação de cenários de abuso relacionados a inteligência artificial.
  • Conhecimento de ransomware, disaster recovery, backups imutáveis e arquiteturas de Data Bunker.
  • Vivência com Zero Trust, shift-left security e modelos que reduzem o blast radius de incidentes.
  • Experiência com build versus buy, definição de roadmaps técnicos e influência sobre padrões adotados por múltiplas equipes.

Buscamos uma pessoa apaixonada por tecnologia, que esteja sempre em busca de novos aprendizados e que goste de desafios. Se você se identifica com este perfil, adoraríamos conhecer você!

Position Summary:

This executive leader is accountable for transforming PointClickCare’s unique data assets, ecosystem position, and network scale into differentiated products, strategic growth opportunities, and new sources of enterprise value.

As a member of the senior Product Leadership Team, the SVP influences corporate strategy, investment priorities, ecosystem partnerships, and growth initiatives while leading a team of senior Product leaders responsible for PointClickCare’s data product portfolio.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Define and lead PointClickCare’s enterprise Data Products strategy, including establishing a multi-year vision for Data as a Product that aligns with corporate objectives, growth priorities, and evolving market opportunities.

  • Lead PointClickCare’s enterprise strategy for data monetization, marketplace growth, and ecosystem expansion.
  • Define customer access models, API strategies, pricing frameworks, packaging approaches, and commercial models that support sustainable growth while preserving trust and protecting intellectual property.
  • Identify new revenue opportunities, strategic partnerships, and ecosystem capabilities that strengthen PointClickCare’s competitive position and expand customer value.
  • Represent PointClickCare’s data strategy with executive stakeholders, customers, strategic partners, industry analysts, and industry organizations.
  • Lead executive-level discussions related to data products, healthcare interoperability, marketplace participation, data monetization, and AI-enabled customer solutions.
  • Build relationships that influence product direction, market positioning, and long-term growth opportunities across the healthcare technology landscape.
  • Lead, develop, and scale a high-performing product leadership organization through senior leaders, including VPs and Directors.
  • Establish succession planning, leadership development, talent strategies, and organizational capabilities that strengthen expertise in data products, APIs, ecosystem platforms, marketplace solutions, and monetization strategies.
  • Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, collaboration, customer focus, and execution excellence.

Required Skills & Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, Healthcare Informatics, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in product management, technology, data products, platform strategy, enterprise software, or related disciplines.
  • Demonstrated success defining and executing enterprise-level product, growth, or business strategies with measurable impact on organizational performance, customer outcomes, and financial results.
  • Proven experience leading large, complex product or technology organizations through multiple layers of leadership, including developing senior leaders and building organizational capability.
  • Track record of leading enterprise transformation initiatives requiring alignment across multiple functions, competing priorities, and significant organizational change.
  • Deep expertise in data products, APIs, interoperability, marketplace and ecosystem strategies, data monetization models, AI-enabled products, and the business dynamics of data-driven organizations.
  • Strong strategic, financial, and operational acumen, including ownership of portfolio-level investment decisions, business cases, risk management, and performance outcomes.

  • Experience leading marketplace, ecosystem, platform, or data monetization strategies is highly preferred.
  • Experience within healthcare technology, post-acute care, payer, provider, or other highly regulated industries is preferred.
  • Experience engaging with industry analysts, strategic partners, customer advisory groups, or external industry bodies is preferred.
  • Ability to balance growth objectives, customer needs, regulatory requirements, and intellectual property protection in a complex business environment.

jobs.description:
The Senior Purchase Card Consultant is responsible for providing leadership, guidance, and technical and regulatory expertise to the Purchase Card Analysts in conducting their oversight role for the NIH Purchase Card Program. Responsibilities also include providing support services to the NIH Agency Program Coordinator and serving as the Team Lead for the On-Site Review Method for assessing compliance to be conducted annually on 10% of the cardholders (CH) and card approving officials (CAO) as described below.

The Senior Purchase Card Consultant is responsible for assisting the NIH Agency Program Coordinator (A/OPC) in the coordination and program administration of various support activities including: revising, updating, and implementing NIH Purchase Card policies and guidelines including updating the NIH Purchase Card Supplement and Standard Operating Procedures and other NIH Purchase Card documentation; attending and assisting with coordinating and planning the monthly NIH Institute and Centers (ICs) Purchase Card Coordinator's Meetings; preparing briefing materials and presentations required by the A/OPC; assisting in special reviews and in documenting and preparing responses to the OMB, the GAO, the GSA, the DHHS, the OIG, the NIH Office of Management and Assessment, and other external and internal entities; assisting the NIH Purchase Card Program Office in developing and updating training materials in accordance with the OMB Circular A-123, Appendix B Charge Card Abuse Prevention Act; assisting with other Purchase Card training not run by the NIH Training Office such as online Refresher Purchase Card Training, Training for NIH IC Purchase Card Coordinators, and training for Card Approving Officials.

The Senior Purchase Card Consultant assists the Senior Manager in developing the monthly report and annual report deliverables required by the NIH Purchase Card Program.

The Senior Purchase Card Consultant is responsible for conducting an annual On-Site Review on 10% of the CHs and CAOs by coordinating and implementing a detailed review of for the selected CHs and CAOs on all purchases made by the respective CH and CAO within a three (3) month period. Briefly, the On-Site Review Method consists of the following:
The major tasks of the Senior Consultant for the On-Site Review Method are:

- Selection and Scheduling of Compliance Reviews: Responsible for providing to NIH a proposed schedule for compliance reviews and obtaining NIH Purchase Card Program approval including any proposed travel.

- Conduct IC Entrance Conference: Responsible for contacting the IC Purchase Card Coordinator to discuss the upcoming reviews within their IC and address any known concerns with the respective IC.

- Perform the Cardholder/Card Approving Official Review: Responsible for performing the reviews using the NIH Purchase Card Checklist and/or CAO Checklist. Document findings of non-compliance by gathering supporting documentation while on-site from CH and/or CAO purchase card files.

- Perform Exit Briefings with Cardholder/Card Approving Official: Responsible for performing an exit briefing with the CH/CAO to discuss preliminary findings and provide justification of proposed findings to be in final report.

- Finalized Review Report: Responsible for preparing and submitting individual standardized letters describing all instances of non-compliance to the NIH Purchase Card Program Office for approval. Responsible for issuing all review reports within 30 calendar days from actual review date.

- IC Debriefing: Responsible for preparing a summary report of the findings and scheduling a briefing to include the IC Purchase Card Coordinator, Contractor and Agency Program Coordinator or COR. Responsible for facilitating and participating in the briefing.

The Senior Purchase Card Consultant must have strong leadership, project management, analytical, compliance assessment and auditing, interpersonal, communications (verbal, written, and presentation), and organizational skills and be able to provide day-to-day planning and operational oversight to the Purchase Card Program Analysts as directed by the Senior Manager.

Must have work experience and knowledge of the FAR, HHS Acquisition Regulation (HHSAR), GSA-Government-wide SmartPay Purchase Card Program, and relevant laws, regulations and agency policies and procedures that govern the NIH Purchase Card Program.

Must demonstrate experience with compliance auditing and be certified in auditing.

The Senior Consultant must possess at least a Bachelor's Degree with at least 8 years of consulting, management, and work experience in procurement and specifically in purchase card programs and oversight of accounting and financial practices, such as described in the the job functions of this position.

Should have a working knowledge of the relevant Federal regulations, policies and guidelines particularly with regards to FAR, GSA, OMB, and DHHS, and also the Government Charge Card Abuse Prevention Act of 2012.

The Senior Consultant must be able to use an approved data analysis tool and comply with NIH OIT Certification and Accreditation (C&A) standards. Significant knowledge and working experience with Microsoft word, excel, relational databases, and data mining and minipulation are required.

  • Business Acumen – understanding and insight into how organizations perform, including business processes, data, systems, and people
