jobs.description:
About Spotted Zebra

At Spotted Zebra, we're building something we genuinely believe in: an AI-native end-to-end hiring platform that helps the world's leading organisations find the right people, faster and fairer than ever before. In short, we're making hiring something everyone loves again - both talent teams and candidates alike.

We're a multi-award-winning Series A company giving talent leaders the solution they've always needed. Skills science native. AI-amplified. Built by people who've lived and breathed TA and knew there had to be a better way.

What we do

Spotted Zebra brings Interview Intelligence, Skills Assessments, and AI Interview Agent together in one powerful platform, designed for intelligence and action. One powerful agent and assistant: Spot. Working the way talent teams need it to, always with humans in control.

The result is talent teams get the insight to predict who will succeed, the speed to move before competitors, the governance to defend every hiring decision, and the capacity to focus on the human moments that matter most.

But our product is only part of the story. Spotted Zebra isn’t just building an AI-native product; we’re building an AI-native company. AI is changing how we build, sell, support customers and make decisions. We use it to move faster, stay closer to customers, reduce unnecessary processes, and give talented people more leverage in their roles.

That means joining Spotted Zebra isn’t just a chance to work on the future of hiring. It’s a chance to help shape what the future of work looks like inside a scaling company: compact, ambitious teams using AI to collaborate better, make decisions quickly, and deliver meaningful impact at speed.

The FTSE100 and Fortune500 companies trusting us include British Airways, NIQ, Domino's, Lidl, Merlin Entertainments, AWE, United Utilities, and Paramount. We've been named Personnel Today's Talent Acquisition Supplier of the Year 2025, secured gold across multiple industry awards, and were recently named on the UK Top 100 Startups List.

But what we’re most proud of is the team. People join Spotted Zebra because the mission is real, the product is genuinely exciting, and the opportunity to shape the future of hiring is huge. What makes it special is the way we work: smart, committed people in compact teams where trust is high, decisions happen quickly, and everyone has the chance to make a visible impact.

If that sounds like the kind of place you want to do your best work - read on.

Our Dazzle (That's Our Team!) 🦓

Fun fact: A group of zebras is called a dazzle – and ours truly is dazzling!

We create a culture in which our team thrives and gallops ahead.

As we roam free and empower our dazzle, we gallop ahead on the journey to achieving our goals. We understand this journey will pose challenges along the way, yet we brighten the trail with our positive mindset and encouragement of others. The dazzle continuously moves, gaining knowledge and skills so that we can graze new grounds.

About the role

Spotted Zebra is growing quickly. With more customers, a larger team and more complex decisions, finance now needs to become a stronger part of how we run and scale the business.

We are looking for a part-time Financial Controller to take on that responsibility, working around two days per week and reporting directly to our CEO. This is a broad and visible role, giving our leadership team and board a clear, trusted view of performance, cash and risk, and helping us make confident decisions.

We already have an outsourced finance partner, established processes and financial models that have supported us to this point. The opportunity now is to build on that foundation, updating and adapting our finance systems, models, controls and processes to reflect where the business is today and where it is going next.

You will bring our accounts, cash flow, budgets and forecasts into a single reliable view of the business, turning the numbers into clear insight for the decisions we need to make.

This is an opportunity to shape how finance works inside a growing company. It will suit someone who enjoys getting into the detail but is equally motivated by improving how the business operates and creating a financial foundation that can scale with us.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Review our existing finance systems, models, controls and processes, then update and adapt them to reflect where the business is today. You will build on what is already in place and make sure it remains reliable and scalable as Spotted Zebra grows.
  • Own the month-end timetable and manage the working relationship with our outsourced finance partner, making sure everyone understands what is needed and when.
  • Review the monthly management accounts in detail, checking revenue, costs, accruals, prepayments, deferred income and other material judgements. You will also identify missing invoices or incomplete information.
  • Resolve issues with the relevant people across Spotted Zebra, maintain a clear action log and make sure corrections are completed before the accounts reach the CEO.
  • Own and maintain our rolling cash-flow forecast, keeping assumptions and actual performance up to date and surfacing risks early.
  • Lead the annual budget and regular re-forecasting process, working with leaders across the business to agree assumptions and explain material variances.
  • Model the cash and profit impact of planned hiring, changes in customer timing, investment decisions and other scenarios, helping the CEO understand the implications and trade-offs.
  • Prepare the financial section of the board pack, including the supporting spreadsheet and slide deck. You will explain performance, cash, runway, forecast, relevant SaaS measures and the main risks or decisions.
  • Oversee commission plans and calculations, make sure approved commission is paid accurately and on time, and support commercial and hiring decisions with clear financial analysis.

What success looks like

Success means monthly accounts are accurate, complete and finalised through a dependable process, with routine issues resolved before they reach the CEO. The cash-flow forecast is current and trusted, and hiring or spending decisions can be modelled quickly.

Within your first 6-12 months, we would expect our finance systems, models, controls and processes to have been reviewed and updated for where the business is today. The budget and re-forecast should have clear ownership across the leadership team, board reporting should be consistent and decision-focused, and commission calculations and other material financial controls should be accurate, documented and completed on time.

Requirements

You'll be a great fit if you ✅

  • Are a qualified accountant, ideally ACA, ACCA or CIMA.
  • Have worked as a Financial Controller or in a comparable hands-on finance role.
  • Have experience in a growing SaaS, technology or other recurring-revenue business.
  • Have strong management accounting skills, including month-end review, accruals, prepayments, revenue recognition and variance analysis.
  • Can build and maintain cash-flow forecasts, budgets and scenario models.
  • Can prepare clear financial information and commentary for boards or senior leadership teams.
  • Are comfortable managing an outsourced bookkeeping or accounting partner while retaining internal ownership of the output.
  • Understand relevant SaaS measures such as ARR, bookings, revenue, gross margin, retention and cash runway.
  • Have strong spreadsheet skills and can improve an existing model without making it unnecessarily complicated.
  • Enjoy investigating a missing invoice or incorrect accrual yourself rather than assuming someone else will catch it.
  • Can communicate financial information clearly and challenge assumptions constructively with senior colleagues.
  • Can work effectively in a part-time role, prioritising the issues that matter while staying close to the business throughout the month.
  • Have experience improving finance systems, models, controls and processes as a company grows.

Nice-to-Haves 🌟

  • Working in a venture-backed scale-up or helping prepare a business for a future funding round.
  • SaaS finance, including recurring revenue, deferred income and multi-year enterprise contracts.
  • Preparing financial board packs, including clear narrative and presentation slides.
  • Reviewing sales commission structures and calculations.
  • Leading annual budgets and maintaining rolling re-forecasts.
  • Working in a start-up or scaling technology company.
  • Coordinating year-end accounts, tax, payroll and other compliance activity with external advisers.
  • Providing commercial decision support for hiring and investment decisions.

Benefits

🤝 Meaningful share options

🏥 Health insurance

💰 Enhanced pension

🍼 Nursery salary sacrifice scheme
🏖️ 25 days holiday, pro rata (excluding bank holidays)
🏠 Remote-first
💻 Work from home budget
🧠 L&D budget
🦷 Dental cover
👀 Eye-care support
🏢 Co-working space budget
🧘 Wellbeing allowance
✈️ Travel insurance

🚗 Electric car scheme

Beyond our core benefits, you'll get access to the latest AI-powered tools and technologies, giving you everything you need to do your best work.

(Some benefits are calculated pro rata based on working hours.)

Our Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

At Spotted Zebra, we welcome people of all stripes. We are committed to providing equal opportunities and an inclusive and diverse culture.

We believe that each and every one of us possesses an extraordinary set of skills and abilities, waiting to be discovered, nurtured, and harnessed for the benefit of all.

We are a team. And no matter your race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, or disability, we will empower you to unleash your superpower to help us create a world where everyone is able to utilise their unique blend of skills and abilities to contribute to the greater good.

Everyone is unique and we encourage you to let us know in your application, or share with your recruiter directly, if there is anything we can do to make your interview experience with us more comfortable and positive.

At Spotted Zebra, everyone is welcome. So even if you don't meet all the requirements, we would still love to hear from you. We are always keen to speak with people who are passionate about our mission.

🦓 Ready to gallop ahead with us? We're a team that moves fast, thinks big, and isn't afraid to challenge how things have always been done. If you're excited about using AI and skills science to transform how the world hires, apply now and a member of our dazzle will be in touch!

Miggo is redefining how organizations protect modern applications. Backed by leading cybersecurity investors and recognized by Gartner® as a Cool Vendor in AI Security, we're building the world's first Application Detection & Response (ADR) platform to help organizations identify exploitable vulnerabilities, stop active attacks, and close the patch gap. Our customers include some of the world's most innovative enterprises, and we're partnering with industry leaders across cloud, security, and observability ecosystems to transform application security. At Miggo, we live by four core principles: make it customer-focused, make it happen, make it better, make it together.

The Role

We're looking for a high-performing Enterprise Account Executive to lead and grow our Southeast enterprise territory. This is not a role for someone looking to manage an existing book of business. We need a builder — someone who thrives in early-stage environments, enjoys creating opportunities from scratch, and can navigate complex enterprise sales cycles involving security, engineering, DevOps, and executive stakeholders. The ideal candidate has experience selling cybersecurity solutions into large enterprises, understands the modern application security landscape, and knows how to leverage partners, cloud providers, and personal networks to generate pipeline and close business.

What you'll do

  • Drive the entire sales process from prospecting through close.
  • Consistently generate pipeline through outbound activity, executive networking, events, referrals, and partner engagement.

  • Lead discovery, business value discussions, POV execution, commercial negotiations, and procurement processes.
  • Partner closely with Sales Engineering to drive technical validation and customer success.
  • Collaborate with Marketing to maximize event, campaign, and content-driven opportunities.
  • Develop strong relationships with strategic partners including AWS, VARs, consultants, MSSPs, and technology alliance partners to create and accelerate opportunities.
  • Represent Miggo at industry conferences, executive events, and customer engagements throughout the territory.
  • Provide market feedback to Product, Marketing, and Leadership teams to help shape company strategy.

What you have

  • 5+ years of enterprise cybersecurity sales experience with a demonstrated track record of exceeding quota.
  • Experience selling AppSec, runtime security, CNAPP, cloud security, DevSecOps, observability, developer tooling, or adjacent cybersecurity solutions.
  • Proven ability to close complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise transactions.
  • Strong understanding of modern application architectures, cloud-native environments, and the challenges facing security and engineering teams.
  • Demonstrated success building pipeline through self-generated activity and partner relationships.
  • Experience working with AWS, cloud marketplaces, channel partners, VARs, or strategic alliances.

  • Based in the Southeast region, with Atlanta, Georgia strongly preferred candidates.

Why Miggo

  • Opportunity to join a rapidly growing cybersecurity company at an inflection point.
  • Category-defining technology solving one of the most important challenges in modern application security.
  • Strong executive team with deep cybersecurity expertise.
  • Backing from top-tier cybersecurity investors.
  • Significant opportunity for career growth, impact, and earnings.

jobs.excerpt: About Nebius:Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy.
jobs.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

This role is for Nebius AI R&D, a team focused on applied research in AI. Examples of applied research that we have recently published include:

  • applying reinforcement learning for agent training in long-context multi-turn scenarios
  • dramatically scaling task data collection to power reinforcement learning for SWE agents
  • building a decontaminated evaluation for SWE agents that is regularly updated
  • investigating how test-time guided search can be used to build more powerful agents

The results often lead to collaboration with adjacent teams where our research findings are applied in practice.

We are currently looking for senior- and staff-level ML engineers to work on research in areas such as:

  • Guided search and reinforcement learning for agentic systems
  • Reinforcement learning for reasoning models
  • Web-scale problem collection for training agents
  • Efficient model distillation

Some examples of what your responsibilities might include are:

  • Conducting experiments to figure out efficient ways to train a large language model on traces of interactions with various environments
  • Exploring methods of guided generation and search in the trajectory space
  • Coming up with ways to mine relevant data at web scale and figuring out efficient ways to use this data in model post-training
  • Conducting experiments with different reinforcement learning configurations in verifiable domains
  • Exploring methods to train AI agents on tasks with non-verifiable reward signals

We expect you to have:

  • A profound understanding of theoretical foundations of machine learning and reinforcement learning
  • Deep expertise in modern deep learning for language processing and generation
  • Substantial experience with training large models on multiple computational nodes
  • Strong software engineering skills (we mostly use python)
  • Deep experience with modern deep learning frameworks (we use jax)
  • Strong communication and leadership abilities
  • Experience designing, executing, and analyzing machine learning experiments with proper statistical rigor
  • Ability to formulate research questions, design experiments to test hypotheses, and draw meaningful conclusions from results
  • Ability to document research findings clearly and contribute to technical publications or report

Nice to have:

  • Experience with deep reinforcement learning for LLMs, including techniques such as reward modeling, DPO, PPO etc
  • Familiarity with important ideas in LLM space, such as RoPE, ZeRO/FSDP, Flash Attention, quantization
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a related field Master’s or PhD preferred
  • Track record of building and delivering products (not necessarily ML-related) in a dynamic startup-like environment
  • Experience in engineering complex systems, such as large distributed data processing systems or high-load web services
  • Open-source projects that showcase your engineering prowess
  • Excellent command of the English language, alongside superior writing, articulation, and communication skills
  • Proficiency in contemporary software engineering approaches, including CI/CD, version control and unit testing

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

Equal Opportunity Statement:

Nebius is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace and to providing equal employment opportunities in all aspects of employment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the country in which they apply and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility as a condition of hire.

jobs.excerpt: About UsInStride Health’s mission is to deliver specialty anxiety and OCD care that works for every kid, teen, young adult, and family who needs it.
jobs.description:
About Us

InStride Health’s mission is to deliver specialty anxiety and OCD care that works for every kid, teen, young adult, and family who needs it. Through this mission, we are expanding access to insurance-based care, increasing engagement in treatment, and improving treatment outcomes. We are doing this by combining research-backed clinical care and innovative technology to eliminate the major problems with care today: difficulty finding providers, months of waiting to be seen, arduous onboarding processes, and inconsistent use of evidence-based therapies and outcomes tracking. Our vision is to become the nation’s most trusted provider of pediatric anxiety and OCD care.

TeamInStride Health: Our Core Values

  • Give Heart: We lead with heart, treating patients and their families the way we want our loved ones to be treated.
  • Work Smart: We find smarter ways to solve hard problems and fix the broken mental health system by leveraging technology, diversity of thought, and innovation.
  • Have Humility: We leave our egos at the door, empowering our team to collaborate, celebrate diversity, and adopt a growth mindset.
  • Embrace Community: We all belong. We are in this together, and we never worry alone. We believe in each other and recognize that every voice matters.

About the Role

We are looking for a virtual Child & Adolescent Therapist to join our team to deliver family-centric and evidence-based care. This is a fully remote position.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide evidence-based individual and group treatment to patients and families
  • Use measurement-based care to inform treatment planning
  • Collaborate with other care team members (e.g., coach and psychiatrist)
  • Provide feedback on program curricula and training protocols
  • Provide feedback regarding the various applications of technology in treatment
  • Maintain awareness of risk management issues
  • Complete documentation in a timely and thorough manner
  • Participate in initial and ongoing trainings on the application of evidence-based and tech-enhanced care delivery
  • Facilitate skills or skills practice groups, as assigned. These age-based groups, for patients or parents/caregivers, focus on skills development and implementation based on the InStride Health curriculum. These groups are based in CBT, and integrate aspects of ACT and PMT

What You Need to Succeed in the Role

  • Ph.D. or PsyD. in psychology from an accredited school of psychology, LCSW from an accredited school of social work, or LMHC & Masters degree from an accredited graduate program
  • New York licensure appropriate to clinical discipline
  • Strong background in treating children and adolescents with anxiety and related disorders
  • Experience and training in delivering evidence-based treatments (e.g., CBT, ACT, DBT)
  • Basic computer skills, facility with and openness to new technologies
  • Excellent written and interpersonal communication skills
  • Ability to be flexible and nimble and work well both independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced, mission driven environment
  • Culturally responsive with regard to diversity and inclusion
  • Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information in a manner that inspires confidence and trust

The expected annual salary for this role is between $85,000-95,000. Actual starting salary will be determined on an individualized basis and will be based on several factors including but not limited to specific skill set, work experience, licensure, etc. Additional compensation may be considered based on factors such as licensure type, appropriate state licensure, prime time hour availability, and more.

Why Join Our Team

  • Generous benefits package (401k with match, Flexible PTO, paid holidays, paid service days, 4 week paid sabbatical, 12 week paid parental leave, health benefits starting on your first day, and more)
  • Opportunity to join a mission-driven company that is changing the landscape of pediatric mental health treatment
  • Chance to make a far-reaching impact by helping children and families access desperately-needed, evidence-based care
  • Opportunity to work with talented and experienced team members who have devoted their lives to solving this problem
  • Fully virtual: work from the comfort of your home with periodic in-person retreats

Commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, & Belonging (DEIB)

We want to make our clinical services available for everyone, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or how you identify. To achieve this, we recognize we must continually make progress in building a more diverse, equitable, and inclusive team. Through these efforts, we support two primary objectives at InStride Health:

  1. Providing high quality patient care to families. We are in a privileged position to support families during a vulnerable time in their lives. We approach all families and each other with compassion and are most effective as a diverse team where all individuals feel valued, respected, and accepted.
  2. Building a mission-driven business that lasts. Specifically, we believe our commitment to a supportive culture improves innovation, decision-making, and efficiency.

We invite you to share any additional information about yourself or your experiences that may not be reflected in your CV. Inclusion of this information is completely voluntary.

Beware of fake job postings and offers. All official communications from InStride Health will come from email addresses ending in @instride.health. We will never ask for personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank details during the application process. If you receive a suspicious job offer or communication, please contact our recruitment team directly () to verify its authenticity.

  • Strong judgment and the confidence to offer recommendations, raise concerns, and respectfully challenge assumptions when market information points to a different approach.
  • Clear, engaging written and verbal communication with candidates and colleagues at different levels of an organization.

  • Experience using recruiting data, sourcing results, candidate feedback, and market information to assess effectiveness and guide decisions.
  • Proficiency with an Applicant Tracking System and recruiting technology. Experience with SmartRecruiters is a plus.
  • Comfort working in a decentralized environment where teams may have different business needs, processes, priorities, and decision-making styles.
  • A collaborative, curious approach and the ability to build influence through trust rather than formal authority.

Work Environment and Flexibility

This is a work-from-home position, not a location-independent position. Candidates must be based in the United States and able to work standard business hours aligned with the Pacific or Mountain Time Zones. Team members who live near a KPFF office may have the option to work onsite or in a hybrid arrangement. Occasional travel for team meetings, recruiting activities, and office visits may be required.

Compensation

Final compensation will be determined based on the depth and relevance of the candidate's recruiting experience, including experience within architecture, engineering, construction, consulting, or related technical talent markets; demonstrated success leading complex searches; geographic location; and other job-related qualifications.

  • 401(k) Retirement Plan: KPFF contributes 3% of salary with no employee contribution required.

  • Paid Time Off: PTO, two floating holidays, and paid company holidays.

jobs.excerpt: Who We Are:Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 10 million brokerage accounts.

Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Your Role:

We are looking for a Total Rewards leader who is deeply fluent in compensation and equally energized by the analytical, cross-functional work that comes with building a growing company.

This is a hands-on Manager / Senior Manager role. Compensation is the center of gravity, not the whole job. You will own core Total Rewards work across a global, remote workforce, and you will also take on high-impact People work including headcount planning, people budgeting, and M&A from a People / Total Rewards lens — plus other analytical projects that sit outside a traditional TR box. Those projects will often be analytical: turning messy data into decisions, standing up new processes, and helping the company scale how we hire, pay, and support people.

You will work across regions, entities, and time zones — not as a single-country specialist. You will partner closely with People, Recruiting, Finance, and business leaders. You will be the person others come to for clean data, sound judgment, and a clear recommendation.

The level (Manager vs. Senior Manager) will be determined by the depth of your experience and the scope you are ready to own.

Things You Get To Do

Total Rewards

  • Own day-to-day compensation programs across a global, remote workforce, including base pay, variable pay, and equity-related processes.
  • Partner with leaders on offers, promotions, leveling, and pay decisions so recommendations are consistent, market-aware, and aligned to our philosophy.
  • Build and maintain job architecture, including job IDs, job families, levels, and titles, so hiring, pay, and reporting sit on a clean foundation.
  • Price roles and refresh ranges using multiple market data sources, survey submissions, and internal data. Comfort working across imperfect, overlapping datasets is essential.
  • Run or support compensation cycles (merit, bonus, equity, and related processes), including modeling, manager enablement, quality checks, and close-out reporting.
  • Implement, configure, and support compensation platforms and related tools. You do not need to have used a specific vendor; you do need to have stood up or been a primary operator of a compensation system, and to keep it accurate as the company changes.
  • Advise on global benefit structures and how they interact with total rewards. You will not be expected to be a benefits administrator in every country, but you should understand how benefit design, eligibility, and cost differ across markets and be able to partner with specialists, brokers, and vendors.
  • Support pay equity, pay transparency, and related compliance work with practical analysis and process, not just policy language.
  • Prepare clear materials for People leadership, Finance, and business stakeholders: range recommendations, cycle outcomes, cost models, and “what this means / what we should do.”

Recruiting Partnership

  • Support Recruiting with timely, usable data: ranges, leveling guidance, offer competitiveness, and exception context so offers can move in real time.
  • Maintain job ID integrity as requisitions are opened, backfilled, and re-leveled. Keep the connection between the job catalog and how we hire clean and current.
  • Help Recruiting and hiring managers make consistent decisions when a role does not map neatly to an existing job or market match.

Headcount Planning, Budgeting & M&A

In addition to core Total Rewards, you will:

  • Own or partner on headcount planning with Finance and business leaders: annual plans, in-year changes, backfills vs. new roles, and the connection between the job catalog, reqs, and approved seats.
  • Own or partner on people budgeting: compensation budgets, merit/bonus/equity pool modeling, offer and promotion cost impact, and actuals vs. plan. Build views leadership can use to make decisions.
  • Run scenario work as the company grows or changes shape (hiring pace, mix, location, leveling) so tradeoffs are visible before decisions are locked.
  • Support M&A from a People / Total Rewards perspective: diligence inputs, mapping jobs and pay, comparing compensation and benefit structures, flagging cost and risk, and helping plan integration of people, jobs, and rewards — through close if that is what the work requires.

Key Projects

  • Lead and contribute to People projects that sit adjacent to Total Rewards as Alpaca builds and grows. These will often be analytical and operational: workforce data, process design, program build-outs, integrations, and decision support.
  • Bring a builder’s mindset. You will be asked to go beyond “run the cycle” into questions like how we structure work, how we measure people outcomes, and how we scale programs without adding unnecessary process.
  • Stretch into other People areas as needs emerge. We want someone who is confident in compensation and eager to expand, not someone who wants to stay in a narrow TR lane.
  • Partner across time zones with teammates, vendors, and leaders in multiple countries. Set expectations, document decisions, and keep work moving asynchronously.

Who You Are (Must-Haves)

  • 7+ years of Total Rewards, compensation, or closely related People analytics/operations experience, including ownership of compensation programs in a multi-country or globally distributed environment. Manager vs. Senior Manager will depend on the depth and breadth of that ownership.
  • Strong compensation craft: job architecture, market pricing, ranges, offer support, pay decisions, and cycle execution. You can explain the “why” behind a recommendation, not just the number.
  • Experience managing multiple compensation data sets and surveys: submissions, matching, aging, blending sources, and reconciling conflicts between vendors, geographies, and internal history.
  • Hands-on experience implementing and/or serving as a primary operator of a compensation platform (planning, job/range data, workflow, or similar). Specific vendors are less important than having done the work.
  • Working knowledge of benefit structures across multiple countries — eligibility, typical plan design differences, and how benefits sit inside a total rewards package.
  • Proven partnership with Recruiting: providing real-time range, leveling, and offer data; keeping job IDs accurate; and helping hiring move without sacrificing consistency.
  • Ability to own headcount planning and people budgeting, plus comfort operating in M&A-style analysis even without a deal-team background.
  • High analytical fluency. You are comfortable in spreadsheets and people data, can build models others can follow, and can turn analysis into a short, clear recommendation.
  • Experience working across global locations and time zones. You communicate clearly in writing, document decisions, and do not need everyone in the same room to make progress.
  • Sound judgment and discretion with sensitive pay, offer, and employee data.
  • Builder energy: you like standing up something that did not exist, improving a messy process, and then operating it well. You are grounded in compensation and genuinely interested in stretching into other People work.
  • Ability to overlap with West Coast working hours on a regular basis. Pacific, Mountain or Central time zone bases preferred.

Who You Might Be (Nice-to-Haves)

  • Direct prior M&A experience from a People / Total Rewards lens (due diligence, mapping jobs and pay, integration planning, or post-close alignment). The work is in the job either way; prior deal experience is preferred, not required.
  • Hands-on requisition (req ID) management in partnership with Recruiting: intake, job-to-req mapping, approvals, and data quality.
  • Experience in a high-growth, remote, or multi-entity environment where the org chart, job catalog, and headcount data were changing quickly.
  • Exposure to equity compensation administration or equity cycle support (you do not need to be an equity specialist).
  • Experience partnering on broader People analytics, workforce planning, or HR systems work beyond compensation.
  • Relevant certification (e.g., CCP or equivalent) is a plus, not a requirement.

How We Take Care of You:

  • Competitive Salary & Stock Options
  • Health Benefits
  • New Hire Home-Office Setup: One-time USD $500
  • Monthly Stipend: USD $150 per month via a Brex Card

Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

Lumen is seeking an experienced GTM Systems Administrator specializing in LeanData to lead the administration, governance, optimization, and evolution of our Lead-to-Revenue operations platform. This role will be responsible for configuring and maintaining LeanData to support enterprise lead routing, account matching, queue management, buying group orchestration, meeting scheduling, and revenue process automation across multiple Salesforce environments.

The GTM Systems Administrator will partner closely with Marketing Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Campaign Operations, Demand Generation, and Salesforce teams to design scalable processes that improve speed-to-lead, routing accuracy, operational efficiency, and pipeline performance.

The ideal candidate combines strong platform administration skills, deep understanding of lead management processes, and a passion for building intelligent, automated customer journeys that support business growth.

Work Location

Fully remote position open to candidates based anywhere in the U.S.

The Main Responsibilities

Platform Administration & Governance

  • Administer and maintain the LeanData platform, including routing logic, matching rules, FlowBuilder configurations, BookIt scheduling, Insights, orchestration workflows, and governance standards.
  • Configure and support lead, contact, account, opportunity, and buying-group orchestration processes.
  • Establish and maintain routing governance, naming conventions, documentation, and operational best practices.
  • Monitor platform health, performance, and adoption to ensure reliable and scalable operations.
  • Conduct periodic audits of routing logic, ownership rules, queues, and matching configurations.

Lead Management & Revenue Process Optimization

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Facilitate stakeholder discussions to align routing strategies with business priorities and go-to-market objectives.
  • Serve as the primary subject matter expert for LeanData capabilities and roadmap planning.

Reporting & Analytics

  • Develop dashboards, reports, and operational insights that measure routing effectiveness, SLA compliance, conversion performance, and operational health.
  • Analyze trends and performance metrics to identify opportunities for optimization.
  • Provide recommendations backed by data to improve lead management and funnel efficiency.
  • Support leadership reporting and quarterly business reviews.

Integration & Technology Management

  • Collaborate with Salesforce, Adobe, Marketo, Demandbase, ZoomInfo, Conversica, and other MarTech platform owners to ensure seamless integration and data flow.
  • Support testing, deployment, and ongoing maintenance of new capabilities and integrations.
  • Assist with data governance initiatives, process documentation, and operational readiness planning.
  • Evaluate new features and platform enhancements to continuously improve capabilities.

User Enablement & Support

  • Provide training, documentation, and guidance to platform users and stakeholders.
  • Troubleshoot routing, matching, scheduling, and automation issues.
  • Maintain knowledge articles, runbooks, and process documentation.
  • Drive adoption through education, communication, and best-practice recommendations.

What We Look For in a Candidate

  • 3–5+ years of experience administering LeanData, Salesforce, Revenue Operations, Marketing Operations, or a related GTM technology platform.
  • Strong understanding of lead lifecycle management, lead routing, account matching, and sales process automation.
  • Experience supporting complex Salesforce environments and cross-functional business processes.
  • Experience configuring workflow automation and business process rules.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate business requirements into scalable technical solutions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Salesforce Administrator certification.
  • Experience with Marketo, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Real-Time CDP, Demandbase, ZoomInfo, Conversica, or other enterprise GTM technologies.

  • Knowledge of integrating SAFe and Kanban approaches to optimize flow and delivery predictability is considered as an asset;
  • Excellent command of the English language.

Responsibilities

  • Organize and facilitate agile activities and ceremonies including daily stand-up meetings, sprint reviews, retrospectives, sprint and release planning, and product backlog refinement sessions;

  • Collaborate closely with the product owner to manage the backlog;
  • Coach team and Product Owner on empiricism, value‑based backlog slicing, and incremental delivery;
  • Track and radiate flow metrics (velocity, sprint burndown, iteration burn rate) and guide the team in data‑driven improvement;

  • Promote empowered, self‑organising teams, shared vision, psychological safety, collaborative decisions (e.g., Fist‑of‑Five);
  • Uphold Definition of Done, quality gates, and compliance with organisational standards;
  • Communicate with other SCRUM masters and product owners across the organization to ensure transparency into delivery progress, challenges, and risks;
  • Utilize team feedback and metrics (e.g., quality, delivery, cadence, etc.) to identify areas of opportunity and work with team to continuously improve;
  • Support the team in using agile planning and development tools (e.g. Azure DevOps, Confluence);
  • Experiment with new practices and frameworks to improve team outcomes;
  • Actively participate in learning opportunities such as communities of practice or conferences to improve skills and better support the team;
  • Contribute to the advancement and improvement of agile practices within the organization.

Arcadia is dedicated to happier, healthier days for all. We believe that there is a better healthcare world – one powered by data. Our platform transforms complex, diverse data into a unified foundation for health, helping organizations deliver better care, boost revenue, and lower costs.

Why This Role Is Important to Arcadia

At Arcadia.io, the Customer Success Manager (CSM) has complete responsibility for end-to-end customer success for Arcadia’s non-enterprise clients. CSMs commit to the ongoing work of making satisfied customers, through ensuring collective adoption of Arcadia capabilities, strong data quality, rapid and effective support, and smooth upgrades. The CSM displays an intimate understanding of Arcadia functionality and can marry this understanding with their knowledge of value-based care to lead product training, mitigate issues, and reconfigure tools to meet new business goals. A CSM’s experience and skills enable them to independently manage a portfolio of customer accounts operating as the clients’ primary point of contact. CSMs build long term relationships with their clients and are vested in their success.
CSMs have a knack for connecting strategic business objectives to Arcadia’s capabilities, enjoy getting into the weeds, and excel at critical problem solving. The CSM leads cross-functional teams to effectively troubleshoot, and project manage complex technical issues. As the customer’s primary point of contact, the CSM will prioritize executing projects to support each client’s business objectives, increasing the adoption of Arcadia tools and capabilities, manage post-initial implementation projects, communicate timelines, and be the first line of expertise and support for Arcadia customers.
In this position, you will work closely with division leaders, implementation management, production support SMEs, engineering, product managers and service desk teams.

What You'll Bring

About Us:

OncoveryCare is an early-stage virtual healthcare company committed to fundamentally rethinking and transforming the landscape of physical and mental healthcare for cancer survivors. Our team is composed of cancer survivors, clinicians, and experts in cutting-edge healthcare delivery. We believe that world class care after a cancer diagnosis shouldn’t end when treatment is over, and we provide an innovative, evidence-based approach to deliver patient-centered, whole-person support for survivors throughout the cancer journey.

Our vision is a world where living beyond cancer isn’t just “surviving”—it’s thriving.

A few tidbits about cancer survivorship:

  • There are over 18 million cancer survivors in the United States today—and that number is expected to grow to 26 million by 2040
  • Cancer survivors experience a range of physical and mental health side effects from treatment
  • Survivorship starts at the moment of diagnosis and continues post-treatment—we are starting in the “transitions of care” phase post-treatment, when there is often not a specialized team to take over caring for the survivor moving forward

Our Guiding Principles:

  • By survivors, for survivors: We build the survivor voice and experience into all that we do
  • Clinical integrity and rigor: We prioritize evidence-based approaches and an integrated team to deliver the highest-quality care
  • Trauma-informed care: We “meet survivors where they are” and respect their lived experience
  • Changing the status quo: We are committed to radically reinventing how cancer survivorship care is designed, delivered, and experienced
  • Transparency & inclusivity: Building a new frontier of cancer care is both hard and rewarding—everyone has a role to play, and fostering a positive and open team culture is our priority

Position Summary

The Executive Director or Senior Director, Medical Affairs, is responsible for developing and executing Medical Affairs strategy aligned with Nektar’s corporate objectives, clinical development priorities, and product lifecycle needs. The role will establish the capabilities, processes, and partnerships required for evidence generation, Investigator-Sponsored Trials, scientific engagement, medical education, publications, field medical strategy, and launch readiness.

This leader will help build and lead Medical Affairs capabilities to support the Nektar pipeline and will partner with corporate leadership and cross-functional teams to align priorities across the organization. The position will also establish strategic relationships with medical societies, patient advocacy organizations, academic centers, healthcare professionals, clinical sites, investigators, and other external scientific experts. The successful candidate will be a hands-on leader who can operate effectively in a dynamic biotechnology environment while simultaneously building long-term Medical Affairs capabilities and infrastructure.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Medical strategy and execution

•Lead implementation of the Medical Affairs strategy for rezpegaldesleukin in atopic dermatitis and alopecia areata, converting strategic priorities into integrated plans for evidence generation, external scientific engagement, scientific communications, medical education, publications, field medical execution, and launch readiness.

•Provide senior leadership and strategic direction for the Medical Affairs function, establishing priorities, operating plans, governance, and measures of success aligned with corporate objectives, R&D priorities, and product lifecycle needs.

Organization and people leadership

•Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Medical Affairs organization, including the field medical team; oversee workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding, performance management, coaching, training, succession planning, and professional development.

External scientific engagement

•Develop and lead strategic relationships with clinical investigators, external scientific experts, medical societies, patient advocacy organizations, academic centers, healthcare professionals, clinical sites, and other relevant stakeholders to inform development and Medical Affairs priorities.

•Plan and lead steering committees and Medical Affairs advisory boards for Nektar programs, translating external input into actionable recommendations for evidence generation, scientific engagement, and lifecycle strategy.

Evidence generation and scientific communications

•Provide Medical Affairs leadership for evidence-generation activities across phases I through IV, including study-concept development, external scientific input, investigator engagement, and appropriate support of study awareness and enrollment initiatives.

•Partner closely with Clinical Development, Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacovigilance, Commercial, Market Access, Medical Information, Corporate Communications, and Business Development to align evidence generation, scientific communications, launch readiness, and lifecycle strategy.

•Serve as a credible scientific and medical representative of the company, engaging healthcare professionals and external experts in balanced, evidence-based, and compliant scientific exchange.

•Provide medical and scientific leadership for launch readiness, appropriate clinical adoption, and lifecycle planning based on unmet need, available evidence, and insights from the evolving treatment landscape.

•Lead the development of nonpromotional medical and scientific materials and provide Medical Affairs input into promotional review and training in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and company policies.

•Lead and support publication strategy and execution for clinical studies, evidence-generation initiatives, and other relevant scientific activities, ensuring scientific accuracy, transparency, and adherence to applicable publication standards.

•Maintain current knowledge of the treatment landscape, scientific literature, medical developments, and competitive intelligence; translate relevant insights into Medical Affairs strategy and communicate them effectively to cross-functional colleagues.

•Demonstrated ability to solve complex problems with innovative solutions.

•Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

•Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

•Proven experience working effectively with senior management.

•Experience conducting formal presentations to Senior Management and key opinion leaders.

•Knowledge of effective competitive strategies.

•In-depth understanding of clinical product development in the pharmaceutical industry.

•Strong analytical skills, especially regarding the interpretation of scientific research and literature.

•Understanding of clinical data-analysis methodologies.

•Initiative and strong interpersonal collaboration skills.

•Strong matrix leadership and strategic influence competency.

Education Requirements

•An advanced doctoral degree (MD, PharmD, PhD, or equivalent) in a scientific, medical, or health-related discipline is required.

Experience Requirements

Leveling will be based on the candidate’s depth of experience and demonstrated leadership scope. Senior Director candidates should have a strong record of independently leading major Medical Affairs programs and influencing cross-functional strategy. Executive Director candidates should also demonstrate enterprise-level strategic leadership, experience in building or leading Medical Affairs capabilities or teams, and sustained influence with executive leaders and external experts.

·A minimum of 7 years of Medical Affairs experience is required for the Senior Director level, and a minimum of 12 years of Medical Affairs experience is required for the Executive Director level.

·Extensive experience within a headquarters-based Medical Affairs organization is required, including ownership of Medical Affairs strategy, evidence generation, and cross-functional leadership.

·Experience building or scaling Medical Affairs capabilities within an emerging biotechnology company is highly desirable.

·Experience supporting late-stage clinical development programs and launch readiness activities is highly desirable.

·Immunology therapeutic-area expertise is required. Experience in dermatology and/or autoimmune inflammatory diseases is preferred.

Work Location and Travel Requirements

·This position is fully remote within the United States.

·Travel is expected to be up to 40%, including domestic and international travel, to support congresses, advisory boards, investigator meetings, scientific engagement activities, and company meetings.

Working Relationships

This senior-level Medical Affairs role will be expected to work consistently with abstract ideas or situations across functional areas of the business. The position requires in-depth knowledge of the functional area, business strategies, and the company’s objectives and involves interaction with senior-level management both internally and externally.

  • May provide informal mentoring and guidance to newer team members, sharing best practices and product knowledge that helps them grow.
  • Operate independently across shifts and serve as a senior point of reference for peers on complex tickets.

What Will Set You Up For Success

Relevant backgrounds include technical support, customer success, implementation, IT, QA, restaurant operations, or other roles requiring strong troubleshooting and customer communication. Direct experience with online ordering, payment integrations, POS systems, or marketing automation preferred.

Job Title: Principal Learning Experience Designer, Adolescent Literacy Intervention

Location:Remote (US)

What you'll do:

The Principal Learning Experience Designer, Adolescent Literacy Intervention will play a critical role in shaping the instructional vision and evolution of Read 180, a leading intervention solution for students in grades 3–12. This individual will bring deep expertise in adolescent literacy, reading intervention, and learning experience design to develop cohesive teacher-led and student-facing experiences across print and digital environments.

As a senior instructional leader, this individual will apply current research in the science of reading and adolescent literacy to develop evidence-based instruction that accelerates literacy growth for students who are reading below grade level. The role will focus on developing comprehension, vocabulary, knowledge building, fluency, and other instructional approaches that help intervention students engage successfully with increasingly complex texts.

The Principal Learning Experience Designer will partner with cross-functional teams to drive the design and continuous improvement of Read 180 learning experiences, while providing guidance, feedback, and mentorship to Learning Experience Designers, and contributing to instructional quality, coherence, and innovation across the program

The Principal Learning Experience Designer will be responsible for the following primary duties:

Adolescent Literacy and Instructional Design

  • Partner with Content and Product leadership to conceptualize and develop evidence-based adolescent literacy instruction for Read 180.
  • Apply current research in the science of reading, reading comprehension, vocabulary, fluency, knowledge building, motivation, and intervention to drive instructional design decisions and product direction.
  • Design cohesive teacher-led and adaptive student learning experiences that provide explicit instruction, meaningful practice, differentiation, and responsive support for diverse student needs.
  • Ensure instructional approaches are appropriate for the cognitive, academic, and social-emotional needs of all adolescent intervention students, including multilingual learners, students with disabilities, and students with varied reading profiles.
  • Contribute to the development of instructional models, lesson architecture, component specifications, and design standards for Read 180.

Content Development and Editorial Quality

  • Write, edit, and revise lessons, instructional routines, student activities, teacher supports, and digital learning experiences for instructional effectiveness and clarity.
  • Lead the selection, development, and refinement of student-facing content, including texts and multimedia resources to support knowledge building, reading engagement, and instructional coherence.
  • Evaluate the relationship among texts, instruction, practice, assessment, and adaptive pathways to ensure a coherent learning experience.
  • Review content developed by internal team members, contractors, and vendors, providing clear and actionable feedback.
  • Maintain high standards for accuracy, consistency, accessibility, inclusivity, and instructional quality across components.
  • Leverage student and teacher feedback, product data, and efficacy findings to identify opportunities to improve instruction.
  • Support the development of content models, metadata, authoring requirements, and reusable instructional structures for digital delivery.

Instructional Leadership and Collaboration

  • Serve as a senior instructional leader and subject-matter expert for adolescent literacy and reading intervention.
  • Partner closely with senior Learning Experience, Product Management, Research, Design, Assessment, and Engineering leaders to establish and execute the instructional vision for Read 180.
  • Guide and mentor Learning Experience Designers, helping them apply literacy research and instructional design principles consistently.
  • Lead instructional reviews, facilitate decision-making, and help the team resolve complex content and learning experience design challenges.
  • Establish models, exemplars, guidelines, and quality criteria that can be applied across the program.
  • Communicate instructional decisions and their research basis clearly to cross-functional partners and senior stakeholders.
  • Work effectively within product development timelines, technical constraints, budgets, and dependencies while protecting the integrity of the instructional experience.
  • Collaborate with researchers, educators, and customers to understand student and teacher needs and validate proposed solutions.

Key Stakeholders/Collaborators

  • Learning Experience and Content Development
  • Product Management and Strategy
  • Literacy Research and Learning Sciences
  • Assessment and Data Analytics
  • Product Design and User Experience
  • Engineering and Technical Product Owners
  • Accessibility and Editorial Teams
  • Professional Services and Customer-Facing Teams
  • External authors, consultants, researchers, and development partners

What you'll need:

  • At least 7 years of experience developing adolescent literacy curriculum, reading intervention solutions, or related instructional products within a publishing, edtech, or curriculum development organization.
  • Demonstrated experience designing cohesive teacher-led and student-facing learning experiences across print, and digital environments across print and digital modalities for students in grades 3–12.
  • Deep knowledge of adolescent literacy development and the needs of students reading below grade level.
  • Strong understanding of current science-of-reading research and its application to older readers, including comprehension, vocabulary, fluency, word recognition, morphology, knowledge building, and motivation.
  • Significant experience designing explicit, scaffolded instruction and intervention for diverse learners.
  • Exceptional instructional writing and editing skills, with the ability to improve content for clarity, engagement, coherence, and effectiveness.
  • Experience leading complex instructional projects and guiding or mentoring other curriculum developers or Learning Experience Designers.
  • Ability to evaluate the quality and alignment of instruction across teacher materials, student materials, assessment, and digital experiences.

Position Summary

Scicom Infrastructure Services is seeking a part-time Strategic Alliances and Partner Manager to manage and strengthen relationships with our technology and ISV partners, including organizations such as Dynatrace, Datadog, Databricks, BigPanda, SpaceX, and other strategic technology providers.

This individual will serve as the primary point of coordination between Scicom and our partner organizations, ensuring that we understand and meet partner program requirements, maintain appropriate certifications and competencies, and take full advantage of available training, sales, technical, marketing, and business development resources.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, proactive, and comfortable working across technical, sales, operations, and executive teams.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage ongoing relationships with Scicom's technology, ISV, and strategic partners.
  • Serve as the primary internal point of contact for partner programs, requirements, initiatives, and communications.
  • Develop a strong understanding of each partner's program structure, certification requirements, competency levels, benefits, and available resources.
  • Maintain documentation of requirements necessary to achieve or maintain partner status, tiers, competencies, or specializations.
  • Track employee training and certification requirements across partner programs.
  • Coordinate with employees and leadership to ensure required partner courses, training programs, and certifications are completed on schedule.
  • Maintain a centralized certification and partner-requirements tracker, including certification expiration and renewal dates.
  • Identify new training and certification opportunities that support Scicom's technical capabilities and strategic objectives.
  • Schedule and participate in regular meetings with partner/channel representatives.
  • Build relationships with partner account managers, channel managers, technical teams, and alliance representatives.
  • Identify partner incentives, rebates, credits, funding programs, marketing resources, training resources, and other benefits available to Scicom.
  • Ensure Scicom is utilizing the full range of resources available through each partner program.
  • Monitor changes to partner programs and communicate relevant requirements or opportunities to leadership.
  • Coordinate completion of partner applications, documentation, renewals, business plans, and compliance requirements.
  • Identify opportunities for joint business development, co-selling, referrals, lead generation, and partner-supported client opportunities.
  • Work with internal leadership to align certifications and partner investments with Scicom's service offerings and growth strategy.
  • Assist with partner portals, opportunity registration, deal registration, certification records, and other administrative partner activities.
  • Provide periodic updates to leadership regarding partner status, certification progress, upcoming requirements, risks, and opportunities.

Qualifications

  • Experience in channel management, strategic alliances, technology partnerships, vendor management, or a related role.
  • Experience working with technology vendors, ISVs, cloud providers, SaaS companies, or IT consulting organizations strongly preferred.
  • Familiarity with partner programs, certification programs, and technology vendor ecosystems.
  • Strong organizational and project-management skills with the ability to manage requirements across multiple partners simultaneously.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-management skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with technical employees, sales teams, executives, and external partner representatives.
  • Strong follow-through and attention to deadlines, certification requirements, and partner program milestones.
  • Comfortable working independently in a consulting or part-time capacity.
  • Experience with partner portals, CRM systems, certification tracking, or similar tools is preferred.

Key Measures of Success

Success in this role will include:

  • Maintaining Scicom's good standing with strategic technology partners.
  • Ensuring required employee certifications and partner competencies are completed and maintained.
  • Increasing utilization of partner training, resources, programs, and incentives.
  • Developing stronger relationships with partner representatives and channel teams.
  • Identifying opportunities that generate new business, technical capabilities, or financial value for Scicom.
  • Providing leadership with clear visibility into the status and value of each strategic partnership.

Position Type

Part-Time Consultant

This position is expected to work independently and collaboratively with Scicom leadership, technical resources, and external technology partners. Hours may fluctuate based on partner initiatives, certification deadlines, and business development activities.

PRIMARY FUNCTION

The Research and Design Fellow- Cultural Landscapes is a term-limited, research- and design-based position for those in fields related to landscape architecture, architecture, engineering, design, or historic preservation. They will complete a project focusing on the cultural landscape of one of Historic New England’s properties with additional assessment on the impacts on that landscape due to climate change. Reporting to the Vice President of Property Care and Climate Action, the Research and Design Fellow- Cultural Landscapes is a member of the Property Care team and collaborates with colleagues across the organization including collections and the visitor experience. The Study Center Manager is a key partner for this position.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

There are two primary focuses of the 2026-2027 project at the Codman Estate in Lincoln, MA. The first is an assessment of the Italian Garden and an assessment of existing conditions and development of recommendations for preservation and restoration. The second is a broader survey of the impacts of weather historically and climate change more recently on the cultural landscape over the years with special emphasis on the trees.

  • Review the historical and contemporary records of the Italian Garden at the Codman Estate and create existing conditions report and plans that document specifically the status of the plantings, the masonry, and the garden objects on the site. Develop recommendations for restoration and preservation of those features with historic authenticity and climate change as the primary considerations. Develop a functional maintenance plan for the garden.
  • Review historical and contemporary records of weather events at the Codman Estate and develop a graphic report noting the impacts over time with special attention to impacted tree communities. Develop recommendations for a replacement plan for Estate regarding the current tree at risk, the Ash tree.
  • Other duties and special projects as assigned to support organizational goals and objectives based on primary project status.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Current enrollment in or completed master’s degree program in a field related to the fellowship topic
  • Experience with and access to CAD or other design software program
  • A strong interest in historic landscapes and knowledge of New England culture and history preferred
  • Means of transportation and ability to travel the New England region
  • New England residency required during the tenure of the fellowship

We are seeking a Data Scientist to join our growing FP&A Solutions team within the Finance Transformation organization. jobs.description:
• Provide The Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition (CFSAN) IT System Lifecycle Development and Management Support Services on behalf of the Food and Drug Association (FDA). The FDA is seeking Small Business (SB) sources to determine the availability and capability of small business manufacturers or small businesses capable of IT System Lifecycle Development and Management Support Services.
  • The FDA | CFSAN is in need of project management services. The Single Award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) will be awarded by the FDA contracting manager. The Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition (CFSAN) is the branch of the United States Food and Drug Administration that regulates food, dietary supplements, cosmetics, drugs, biologics, medical devices, and radiological products.
  • The scope of this contract is to provide the full range of technical and management services necessary to develop, maintain, and enhance CFSAN systems. The general requirements include providing Custom Computer Programming Services (NAICS 541511) to the FDA and CFSAN; and to maintain, support, and evolve code, scripts, views, triggers, jobs, designs, documentation, reports, and templates.
  • There is also a need to establish an ordering vehicle that develops and maintains existing and future Computer to Plate (CTP) systems, which will process structured and unstructured data. The FDA expects between 2-5 new applications/systems to be added to the BPA per year over the duration of this contract. The ProSidian Engagement Team shall provide training services to CFSAN stakeholders for existing applications, application changes, or newly-developed applications. CFSAN will issue individual Task Orders for the Contractor to provide IT Lifecycle Support for the CFSAN IT portfolio of systems as needed. Representative tasks to be performed.

THE BLANKET PURCHASE AGREEMENT IS DIVIDED INTO THE FOLLOWING (9) TASK AREAS:

  • Task 1: Project Management: Task Order level project management to establish control, management, monitoring and notification mechanisms to ensure the individual task orders stay on track to meet the important milestones and performance measures within the awarded task. | DOCUMENTATION: The Contractor shall use FDA supplied templates which will be provided on each individual Task Order as applicable. If an FDA template does not exist, the Contractor may be tasked with drafting a template for approval by the COR.
  • Task 2: O&M and DME Architecture Support Services: The Contractor shall provide the full range of architecture support services in order to formulate the integrated, end-to-end automated systems that provide enhanced IT capabilities necessary to support CFSAN business and mission processes. The goal is a stable evolutionary progression from an organization’s current state to its envisioned future state by identifying tools and technologies that work together to satisfy the needs or changing business needs of the CFSAN users.
  • Task 3: Development, Modernization, and Major Enhancement: The Contractor shall provide the complete range of system development lifecycle support services necessary to develop and enhance CFSAN IT systems and tools as well as their external interfaces to FDA Enterprise and Center Systems and applications. Tasks may encompass the complete lifecycle of activities required for database, application and tool development including, but not limited to requirements elicitation, analysis and validation; system design; code generation; testing; deployment; and documentation. The Contractor shall also develop, support and evolve designs, customizations and process automation such as interfaces, templates, scripts, workflows, interfaces to permit reviewer access to analytics/tools, and reports. Deliverable products shall be validated and tested to ensure that they meet applicable/specified standards, policy, business requirements.
  • Task 4: Systems Integration and Engineering Services: The Contractor shall support CFSAN with integration services. The Contractor shall focus on the development and deployment of integrated information systems that reflect the introduction of a Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) orientation and, moreover, places an emphasis on the recommended acquisition and re-use of existing components—be they FDA components, HHS components, or components acquired from any other source.
  • Task 5: Data Migration and Management Support: The Contractor shall provide data management support for activities related to the development and execution of data architectures, data policies, practices, and procedures that properly manage the full data lifecycle needs of CFSAN. Task #6 - Operations and Maintenance (O&M) and Support Services
  • Task 6: Operations and Maintenance (O&M) and Support Services: The Contractor shall provide the complete range of operations and maintenance support services necessary to maintain CFSAN IT systems. The Contractor shall be responsible for maintaining the “lights on” availability, reliability, and security of the CFSAN IT portfolio through the full range of O&M services. The Contractor shall maintain, support, and evolve code, scripts, views, triggers, jobs, designs, documentation, reports, and templates. The Contractor shall analyze and report on the impact of infrastructure, software upgrades, capacity, and all changes to the technical environment. These day-to-day operations, maintenance, and help desk support ensures that the systems perform their intended functions.
  • Task 7: System and Data Disposition: The Contractor shall identify, recommend and implement the retirement and consolidation of systems, components, technologies, tools and data when they meet the appropriate disposition stage of the lifecycle as defined in the EPLC.
  • Task 8: Training Support for O&M and DME: The Contractor shall provide training services to CFSAN stakeholders for existing applications, application changes, or newly developed applications. The Contractor shall assess the level of capability of the users and the need for training. The Contractor shall prepare a training plan, the training materials, and arrange and conduct training sessions. The training plan and materials shall be provided to the COR for review and approval prior to training.
  • Task 9: Transition Activities: The Contractor shall provide the transition-in and transition-out of activities to develop, operate, and manage the CFSAN IT portfolio. It is the responsibility of both the incoming Contractor and outgoing Contractor to ensure a smooth transition, with minimal disruption to services and support for users. The purpose of the transition is to transfer expert knowledge, data, and artifacts that are used to support applications from the incumbent Contractor to the successor Contractor efficiently.

*** Enterprise Performance Lifecycle (EPLC) Agile Methodology: The Food and Drug Administration maintains a project management methodology framework that incorporates best government and commercial practices through a consistent and repeatable process, and provides a standard structure for planning, managing and overseeing IT projects over their entire life cycle. The HHS Enterprise Performance Life Cycle (EPLC) framework provides that methodology for HHS OPDIVs including FDA.

TEAM PROSIDIAN PERSONNEL SHALL HAVE EXPERIENCE IN THE FOLLOWING:

  • Expertise and experience in designing, developing, implementing, communicating, administering and evaluating human resources programs, with emphasis in compensation and classification in large (i.e., over 4,000 employees) geographically dispersed organizations with a technical, multi-faceted mission of national scope.
  • Demonstrated successful experience in designing and implementing innovative private and public sector compensation and pay for performance programs, and/or expertise in a unionized environment.
  • Experience in job analysis and evaluation, with expertise in making accurate Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) exemption determinations, and demonstrated ability to successfully defend those decisions to employees, management, and/or outside parties.

  • Knowledge of existing laws and regulations pertaining to the federal compensation, classification, performance, and recognition programs, and to the federal financial regulatory agencies.

PROJECT MANAGER – KEY PERSONNEL QUALIFICATIONS:

Takes projects from original concept through final implementation. Interfaces with all areas affected by the project including end users, computer services, and client services.
